data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FlightAware的MiseryMap及其他相关工具的使用和价值

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  • [er0k]：认为FlightAware的MiseryMap很酷，并提供了链接。
  • [nunez]：对MiseryMap和fly.faa.gov/ois在处理地面延误时的实用性表示肯定，并推荐了ExpertFlyer，认为其对于频繁旅行者非常有价值，尤其是重新订票和换座。
  • [sklargh]：强调MiseryMap在延误时提供的信息优势，帮助做出替代交通方式或放弃行程等决策。
  • [ZeWaka]：经常使用MiseryMap，认为其能在航空公司做出决定前预知延误，并推荐使用'Map View'和'Weather'标签。

• [疑问和困惑]
  • [robertclaus]：观察到SFO、DEN、LAS和EWR机场因天气延误，质疑是否繁忙机场更容易延误，或只是当天运气不好。
  • [pavelstoev]：对YYC（卡尔加里，加拿大）出现在美国.gov网站上表示困惑，质疑是否遗漏了什么。
  • [VectorLock]：询问BOS（波士顿）关闭的原因。

补充讨论：
• 工具的价值和使用场景：多个评论强调MiseryMap和其他工具在旅行延误时的实用性，特别是在需要快速决策时。
• 对机场和天气影响的关注：一些用户关心特定机场的延误情况和天气对机场运作的影响。
• 技术和数据来源的疑问：有用户对机场代码出现在特定国家网站上以及某些机场关闭的原因表示困惑，反映出对工具数据来源和技术细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• 机场延误的原因及是否繁忙机场更容易延误：[robertclaus]提出了对繁忙机场延误频率的疑问，但未有明确解答。
• 数据和信息的准确性和来源：[pavelstoev]对机场代码出现在美国政府网站上感到不解，这涉及到工具数据整合的准确性和来源问题。

data.title: Tarpit ideas: What they are and how to avoid them (2023) [video]
data.author: dgs_sgd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：什么是“ tarpit idea”（陷阱想法），以及如何识别和应对这些想法

不同观点：
• **Kristopolous的观点**：技术或商业想法的成功往往依赖于环境的变化。许多现在成功的技术（如YouTube、AI、电动汽车等）都经历了多次失败，直到技术、数据或市场条件成熟。因此，识别环境变化和时机是关键，以前失败的想法可能在条件成熟后变得可行。

• **Cjs_ac的观点**：在教育技术（EdTech）领域，很多想法被视为陷阱想法。教师行业有严格的职业标准和持续的专业发展要求，许多EdTech工具只是一时的潮流，无法形成稳定的商业模式。如果要向学校销售软件，应该关注行政管理问题，而不是课堂教学工具。

• **Asimpleusecase的观点**：陷阱想法在事后看来很明显，但对创始人来说难以识别。VC（风投）可以通过失败经验识别陷阱想法，但创始人可以通过深入研究、确保产品有收入来源、避免烧钱来降低风险。陷阱想法有可能在条件变化后变成蓝海机会。

• **Davidedicillo的观点**：有些想法注定只是个人爱好项目，创始人需要有清醒的认识。例如，书签服务不太可能成为大规模商业项目，但仍然有个人价值。

• **FinnLobsien的观点**：YC（Y Combinator）关注的是潜在的巨大市场项目，许多典型的陷阱想法（如待办事项应用、习惯追踪器等）可能对小团队来说是好生意，但不具备大规模市场的潜力。

• **Bob1029的观点**：B2C（企业对消费者）项目比B2B（企业对企业）项目更难成功。B2C需要持续的市场营销投入，而B2B一旦建立客户关系，可以大幅降低营销成本。

• **Dzink的观点**：YC聚集了大量失败的经验，但没有充分公开这些信息。如果能够公开失败的想法和方法，可以更好地引导新创始人探索新的机会，从而提高VC（风投）的回报。

• **Scene_Cast2的观点**：有些想法在技术条件成熟前是陷阱想法。例如，室内WiFi/BLE定位技术在过去存在问题，但现在有了更精确的API和解决方法。

• **Debarshri的观点**：有些陷阱想法因为创始人的执行力而成功，最终可能带来巨大的回报。创业本身就像一个陷阱想法，需要 perseverance（坚持）和勇气去渡过难关。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了具体领域（如EdTech、AI、B2C/B2B）中的陷阱想法例子，以及识别和应对这些想法的策略。
• 强调了研究失败案例、确保收入来源、关注行政管理问题等具体方法，以避免陷入陷阱想法。
• 有人提出YC本身可能是问题的一部分，因为它没有充分利用其失败经验来帮助新创始人。

争议焦点：
• 关于EdTech领域是否存在大量陷阱想法，以及这些想法是否只是一时潮流，存在争议。
• 关于B2C和B2B项目的相对难度和成功潜力，存在不同看法。
• 关于YC是否充分利用其资源和失败经验来帮助新创始人，存在质疑。

data.author: gnabgib

主要讨论点：人工光合作用技术的潜在影响与应用

不同观点：
• ErigmolCt认为，利用无机材料如铜和钙钛矿模拟光合作用，可能是一个潜在的重大突破，如果能够规模化应用，将产生巨大影响。
• Changoplatanero提出，需要比较这种新过程与传统太阳能板发电后合成化学品的效率，以评估其实际效果。
• Krunck强调，应将研究资源集中于这类技术（如人工光合作用和核聚变），以推动科学进步。
• Init7以诗意的方式指出，自然界的叶子具有自我复制和扩展的能力，而人类建造的物品往往在几年内就损坏了。

补充讨论：
• Breggles质疑是否应继续生产更多塑料和碳燃料，提出环境影响的问题。
• Noisebuffer以幽默的方式询问是否可以制造像植物机甲移动套装这样的科幻设备。
• Glitchc开玩笑地表示，人类终于可以“翻开新的一页”，随后自行退场。
• Tcdent预测，未来几年我们将通过生物结构实现这些功能，而不仅仅是通过机械操纵无生命材料。

• Junon批评Hacker News上常见的实用主义论调，认为对不实用技术的否定态度过于强烈。

43788053.article_content:
Article
Materials
Key Takeaways
The Liquid Sunlight Alliance is a multi-institutional collaboration working to develop the tools needed to use energy from sunlight to produce liquid fuels.
Researchers built a perovskite and copper-based device that converts carbon dioxide into C
2
products
–
precursory chemicals of innumerable products in our everyday lives, from plastic polymers to jet fuel.
This proof-of-concept research opens new opportunities for energy research.
Researchers from the Department of Energy’s Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab) along with international collaborators have brought us one step closer to harnessing the sun’s energy to convert carbon dioxide into liquid fuel and other valuable chemicals. In a recent
publication
in
Nature Catalysis
, the researchers debut a self-contained carbon-carbon (C2) producing system that combines the catalytic power of copper with
perovskite
, a material used in photovoltaic solar panels. This advance builds on over 20 years of research and brings the scientific community one step closer to replicating the productivity of a green leaf in nature.
This work is part of a larger initiative, the Liquid Sunlight Alliance (
LiSA
), which is a Fuels from Sunlight Energy Innovation Hub funded by the U.S. Department of Energy. Led by Caltech in close partnership with Berkeley Lab, LiSA brings together more than 100 scientists from national lab partners at SLAC and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, and university partners at UC Irvine, UC San Diego, and the University of Oregon
.
Researchers involved in this multi-institutional collaboration have made advances in developing our understanding of and the tools needed to develop liquid fuels generated from sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water. (Learn more about the LiSA collaboration in this
roundup
, “Five Ways LiSA is Advancing Solar Fuels.”)
“Nature was our inspiration,” said Peidong Yang, a senior faculty scientist in Berkeley Lab’s Materials Sciences Division and UC Berkeley professor of chemistry and materials science and engineering involved in the published work. “We had to work on the individual components first, but when we brought everything together and realized that it was successful, it was a very exciting moment.”
To build a system that mimics photosynthesis, Yang and his team followed the natural processes that occur in the leaf of a plant. Each individual component of a leaf’s photosynthesizing elements had to be replicated and refined. Tapping into the decades’ worth of research, the scientists used lead halide perovskite photoabsorbers to imitate a leaf’s light-absorbing chlorophyll. And inspired by enzymes that regulate photosynthesis in nature, they designed electrocatalysts made of copper that resemble tiny flowers.
Previous experiments have successfully replicated photosynthesis through the use of biological materials, but this work incorporated an inorganic material, copper. While the selectivity of copper is lower than biological alternatives, the inclusion of copper presents a more durable, stable, and longer-lasting option for the artificial leaf system design.
Work led by researchers in the LiSA project developed the cathode and anode components of the new device. Instruments at Berkeley Lab’s
Molecular Foundry
allowed Yang’s team to integrate the device with metal contacts. During the experiments in Yang’s lab, a solar simulator mimicking a consistently bright sun was used to test the selectivity of the new device.
Prior innovations across research groups enabled an organic oxidation reaction to take place in the photoanode chamber and created C2 products in the photocathode chamber. This breakthrough created a realistic artificial-leaf architecture in a device about the size of a postage stamp
–
it converts CO
2
into a C2 molecule using only sunlight.
The C2 chemicals produced from this device are precursory ingredients for many industries that produce valuable products in our everyday lives
–
from plastic polymers to fuel for larger vehicles that can’t yet run off a battery, like an airplane. Building upon this fundamental research milestone, Yang is now aimed to increase the system’s efficiency and expand the size of the artificial leaf to begin increasing the scalability of the solution.
The
Molecular Foundry
is a user facility at Berkeley Lab.
This work was supported by the
DOE Office of Science
.
###
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
(Berkeley Lab) is committed to groundbreaking research focused on discovery science and solutions for abundant and reliable energy supplies. The lab’s expertise spans materials, chemistry, physics, biology, earth and environmental science, mathematics, and computing. Researchers from around the world rely on the lab’s world-class scientific facilities for their own pioneering research. data.title: Street address errors in Google Maps
data.author: brucedawson
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Google Maps在加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省（BC省）某些地址导航中出现的明显错误。例如，在Vernon市，导航将3207 30th Ave错误地指引到3207 34th Ave，而在温哥华，138 W 6th Ave被定位到距离实际位置2.4公里远的地方，导致一些演员因走错地点而迟到。类似的错误还有1951 W 19th Ave被错误地映射到距离实际位置2.1公里处，以及1355 W 17th Ave被错误地放在不同城市。作者推测这些错误可能是由于打字错误或数据输入问题，并指出Google Maps似乎缺乏对地址和街道布局的基本理解，其数据库可能未进行充分的合理性检查。这些错误显示出Google Maps地址数据库存在缺陷，可能导致用户实际困扰。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Maps地址系统的问题及其全球适用性的挑战

不同观点：
• **aethr**：认为全球物流行业中，地址系统缺乏统一标准，各国甚至各地区都有不同的地址惯例。虽然某些城市可能有明确的地址系统，但像Google Maps这样的全球性产品很难编码和理解所有地区系统。地理编码方案（如what3words）试图解决这一问题，但推广困难。
• **kccqzy**：指出Google Maps的反馈工具可能被恶意使用，错误的地址信息可能被低薪承包商错误处理。以伦敦Elizabeth线的消失为例，说明Google Maps在处理区域信息时可能出现严重错误。
• **brucedawson**：批评Google Maps数据库中存在错误的地址信息，甚至真实建筑被错误定位，导致现实中的困扰。通过博客试图引起Google Maps团队的注意，但问题难以解决。
• **pianom4n**：强调地址中的“城市名称”并不总是与实际城市界限一致，例如SFO的地址在旧金山市区外，纽约皇后区的“城市”通常只是社区。认为对地址应用逻辑分析是困难的。
• **paulmooreparks**：虽然承认Google Maps在全球范围内的任务艰巨且表现值得称赞，但指出其在某些地方（如新加坡）的步行和驾驶指引存在不准确性，需要依赖本地知识来弥补。
• **sleepy_keita**：基于在日本的工作经验，指出Google Maps在城市地址上相对可靠，但在农村地区可能出现重大偏差。
• **nitwit005**：认为任何对地址的假设在实践中都可能不成立，地址系统没有严格的模式，甚至会出现地址消失的情况。
• **bombcar**：怀疑支持国际地址样式和扫描图像中的地址可能会导致混淆，指出街道错误可能源于标记化问题，并询问是否仅限于数字街道。
• **monktastic1**：曾负责Google Maps的数据质量，指出地址问题一直很难解决。Google对数据质量的投资不足，导致问题持续存在。
• **jwr**：主张Google Maps应像公共设施一样受到监管，因为其错误信息对人们的生活产生实际影响。目前的自我修正机制不够及时和有效。
• **misswaterfairy**：从事与地址相关的工作，认为地址的不一致性是普遍存在的问题，不仅是Google Maps，其他地理编码器也存在误差。
• **precommunicator**：指出Google Maps地理编码API响应中会显示地址类型及其精确度，帮助用户判断地址信息的可靠性。
• **raylad**：观察到Google Maps在旧金山的公共交通指引上出现退步，导致不合理的交通时间膨胀。
• **xnx**：提供实际使用Google Maps的例子，显示不同用户可能得到不同的指引结果。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Google Maps地址系统的全球适用性和准确性，特别是在不同国家和地区的地址惯例差异下如何确保信息的可靠性。
- 用户反馈和自我修正机制的有效性也是讨论的重点，部分用户对Google Maps的错误修正流程表示不满。
- 地址系统的不一致性和复杂性被广泛认同，但不同用户对Google Maps在处理这些问题上的表现评价不一。

43788832.article_content:
I was driving around Vernon, BC a few weeks ago and I asked Google Maps for directions to 3207 30th Ave. It confidently told me where to go but luckily my passenger noticed that it was actually directing me to 3207
34th
Ave, four blocks north. Well that’s odd.
A few days later my cousin asked me (as the
ex-Google
still-nerd member of the family) if I could help with a Google Maps issue. The problem was that the address 138 W 6th Ave in Vancouver was being mapped at a location 2.4 km (that’s 1.5 miles or 123 furlongs) away from the actual location.
I could visualize the absurdity of where it maps the W 6th Ave address by asking Google Maps for directions between 136 W 6th Ave and 138 W 6th Ave. These addresses are adjacent in real life, but Google Maps gave me this:
That’s a long walk to get to the building next door.
There’s another fun way to visualize this bug. Search for “Clark & Page Casting Studios” in Google Maps. Then copy its address, shown in Google Maps, to the clipboard and ask for directions
to
Clark & Page Casting Studios
from
its address. This should be a zero-meter walk, but of course it isn’t. Instead it is, no surprise, a 2.4 km walk from Clark & Page Casting Studios to its address. Fun!
Or this silliness. If you navigate from “138 W 6th Ave Unit 1B” to “138 W 6th Ave #2b” then it is, you guessed it, a 2.4 km walk.
This error was pointed out to me because apparently aspiring actors kept going to the wrong place and being late for their auditions. These mistakes have real-world consequences.
There are more
Finding one error is curious, but two suggests a pattern. I started browsing Google Maps looking for addresses that seemed out of place. I quickly found three more.
1951 W 19th Ave in Vancouver is mapped at a 2.1 km walk from where its address should logically be. It should be in the 1900 block of W 19th Ave but is instead placed ten blocks away by Google Maps:
1355 W 17th Ave, North Vancouver is a particularly odd case because it is mapped as being in the wrong city (in Vancouver instead of North Vancouver), but on the right street (W 17th Ave) but in the wrong block (the 900 block instead of the 1300 block). As it turns out W 17th Ave doesn’t actually exist in North Vancouver. What is going on?
Typos? Street View?
The answer might be typos. 138 W 6th Ave is being mapped at the location where I would expect to find 1038 W 16th Ave located – a pair of single-digit errors. This requires that somebody/something made two errors when entering the address for 1038 W 16th Ave. The problem with this explanation is that 1038 W 16th Ave doesn’t exist – I cycled over there to check and the addresses go straight from 1020 to 1040.
3207 30th Ave in Vernon got a 30 changed to a 34. Maybe that was a typo?
1951 W 19th Ave is mapped where I would expect to find 951 W 19th Ave. This is another single-digit error. This one is less harmful because (again, I cycled over to check) there is no 1951 W 19th Ave, and 1951 and 951 W 19th Ave both map to roughly the same place. If you ask for directions from 951 to 1951 W 19th Ave (which should be ten blocks) you get these 0.0 km directions:
1355 W 17th Ave, North Vancouver is harder to explain. It was mapped adjacent to 979 W 17th Ave, Vancouver. This error severely stretches the definition of “typo” since nothing but the street name is correct (Vancouver and North Vancouver are different cities, separated by Vancouver Harbour).
I also noticed an anomaly in 5 Montcalm St, Vancouver. This address is in the 1300 block of Montcalm so the address makes no sense. I visited this location as well and the building address is actually 1131 W 16th Ave (the house is on a corner) and there is a five on one of the doors on the Montcalm side. Further creeping around the house revealed that there are five units inside the house – the five is a unit number, not a street number! Now I started wondering if a person or AI had seen the five on the door on Montcalm St and assumed that it was an address.
Internals guesswork
The fact that Google Maps can have these errors – that apparently the mapped location of addresses need have no relationship to the layout of the city’s streets – makes it clear that Google Maps has no concept of how street addresses work. There are many rules for how most addresses work in Vancouver but Google Maps appears to have no knowledge of these rules.
It appears that there is an address database somewhere – created by Google Maps, or the cities in BC, or perhaps from Street View data. Somehow that database seems to allow addresses to be mapped to parcels of land and when the address of a parcel of land is entered (by a human being or an AI bot) the database software happily accepts any address and maps it to the parcel, with no sanity checks to make sure it makes sense. Possibly sanity checks that are needed include:
Is the parcel in the geographical bounds of the city name entered?
Is the parcel in the vicinity of the road name entered?
Is the parcel in the

• **misswaterfairy**：从事与地址相关的工作，认为地址的不一致性是普遍存在的问题，不仅是Google Maps，其他地理编码器也存在误差。
• **precommunicator**：指出Google Maps地理编码API响应中会显示地址类型及其精确度，帮助用户判断地址信息的可靠性。
• **raylad**：观察到Google Maps在旧金山的公共交通指引上出现退步，导致不合理的交通时间膨胀。
• **xnx**：提供实际使用Google Maps的例子，显示不同用户可能得到不同的指引结果。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Google Maps地址系统的全球适用性和准确性，特别是在不同国家和地区的地址惯例差异下如何确保信息的可靠性。
- 用户反馈和自我修正机制的有效性也是讨论的重点，部分用户对Google Maps的错误修正流程表示不满。
- 地址系统的不一致性和复杂性被广泛认同，但不同用户对Google Maps在处理这些问题上的表现评价不一。

data.article_summary: 文章探讨了设计伟大性与知名度之间的关系，指出许多优秀设计师可能并不为人知。作者以达·芬奇为例，质疑伟大是否真的如人们想象中罕见，还是只是因为缺乏认可而显得稀少。在当今注意力经济中，社交媒体和奖项往往成为衡量成功的标准，但真正的设计伟大性在于解决问题、满足人类需求，而非知名度。许多卓越设计因其实用性和功能性而“隐形”，不被大众注意。作者强调，设计师的满足应来自工作的完整性，而非外界的认可，提醒人们不应将设计卓越性与知名度混为一谈。

43787676.article_content:
Christopher Butler
Archive
Info
You Can Be a Great Designer and Be Completely Unknown
I often find myself contemplating the greatest creators in history — those rare artists, designers, and thinkers whose work transformed how we see the world. What constellation of circumstances made them who they were? Where did their ideas originate? Who mentored them? Would history remember them had they lived in a different time or place?
Leonardo da Vinci stands as perhaps the most singular creative mind in recorded history — the quintessential “Renaissance Man” whose breadth of curiosity and depth of insight seem almost superhuman. Yet examples like Leonardo can create a misleading impression that true greatness emerges only once in a generation or century. Leonardo lived among roughly 10-13 million Italians — was greatness truly as rare as one in ten million? We know several of his contemporaries, but still, the ratio remains vanishingly small. This presents us with two possibilities: either exceptional creative ability is almost impossibly rare, or greatness is more common than we realize and the rarity is recognition.
I believe firmly in the latter. Especially today, when we live in an attention economy that equates visibility with value. Social media follower counts, speaking engagements, press mentions, and industry awards have become the measuring sticks of design success. This creates a distorted picture of what greatness in design actually means. The truth is far simpler and more liberating: you can be a great designer and be completely unknown.
The most elegant designs often fade into the background, becoming invisible through their perfect functionality. Day to day life is scattered with the artifacts of unrecognized ingenuity — the comfortable grip of a vegetable peeler, the intuitive layout of a highway sign, or the satisfying click of a well-made light switch. These artifacts represent design excellence precisely because they don’t call attention to themselves or their creators. Who is responsible for them? I don’t know. That doesn’t mean they’re not out there.
This invisibility extends beyond physical objects. The information architect who structures a medical records system that saves lives through its clarity and efficiency may never receive public recognition. The interaction designer who simplifies a complex government form, making essential services accessible to vulnerable populations, might never be celebrated on design blogs or win prestigious awards.
Great design isn’t defined by who knows your name, but by how well your work serves human needs. It’s measured in the problems solved, the frustrations eased, the moments of delight created, and the dignity preserved through thoughtful solutions. These metrics operate independently of fame or recognition.
Our obsession with visibility also creates a troubling dynamic: design that prioritizes being noticed over being useful. This leads to visual pollution, cognitive overload, and solutions that serve the designer’s portfolio more than the user’s needs. When recognition becomes the goal, the work itself often suffers. I was among the few who didn’t immediately recoil at the brash aesthetics of the Tesla Cybertruck, but it turns out that no amount of exterior innovation changes the fact that it is just not a good truck.
There’s something particularly authentic about unknown masters — those who pursue excellence for its own sake, refining their craft out of personal commitment rather than in pursuit of accolades. They understand that their greatest achievements might never be attributed to them, and they create anyway. Their satisfaction comes from the integrity of the work itself.
This isn’t to dismiss the value of recognition when it’s deserved, or to suggest that great designers shouldn’t be celebrated. Rather, it’s a reminder that the correlation between quality and fame is weak at best, and that we should be suspicious of any definition of design excellence that depends on visibility. This is especially so today. The products of digital and interaction design are mayflies; most of what we make is lost to the rapid churn of the industry before it can even be lost to anyone’s memory.
The next time you use something that works so well you barely notice it, remember that somewhere, a designer solved a problem so thoroughly that both the problem and its solution became invisible. That designer might not be famous, might not have thousands of followers, might not be invited to speak at conferences — but they’ve achieved something remarkable: greatness through invisibility.
Design greatness is not measured by the recognition of authorship, but in the creation of work so essential it becomes as inevitable as gravity, as unremarkable as air, and as vital as both.

主要讨论点：对浦东机场（PVG）的安检和海关效率的评价

不同观点：
• 观点一：安检和海关效率低下，等待时间过长。有旅客提到国际航班安检排队时间超过一小时，且只有两个安检口开放，导致大量旅客滞留。有人将此问题归因于人手不足或管理不善。
   
• 观点二：部分旅客认为安检和海关程序虽然繁琐，但这是国际大型机场常态，尤其是在疫情期间，安检和防疫措施增加，可能导致时间延长。有人提到其他国家机场也有类似问题，因此认为浦东机场并非特例。

• 观点三：有旅客指出，浦东机场安检和海关的效率问题可能与航班集中到达有关。例如，有人提到早上6-8点之间是多个国际航班集中到达的时间段，导致安检和海关资源紧张。这类观点认为，如果航班到达时间更分散，效率问题会有所缓解。

• 观点四：有旅客对浦东机场的服务态度和设施提出批评，认为工作人员态度不佳、指引不明确，导致旅客困惑和流程缓慢。但也有旅客持相反意见，认为工作人员态度尚可，且设施相对完善，问题主要出在管理层面而非服务质量。

• 观点五：一些旅客认为，浦东机场的硬件设施其实不错，问题主要出在软件和管理上。例如，有人提到自助通关系统不够普及，人工窗口不足，导致效率低下。但也有旅客认为自助设备的使用率已经较高，问题更多在于旅客不熟悉操作流程。

补充讨论：
• 有旅客建议，浦东机场可以借鉴其他国家机场的高效管理经验，例如增加自助通关设备、优化安检口设置、灵活调配人力资源等。

• 争议焦点在于，浦东机场的效率问题是否是管理不善所致，还是由于客观条件如航班集中到达、疫情措施等导致。部分旅客认为机场管理存在问题，而另一些旅客则认为这是全球机场普遍面临的挑战，不应过分苛责浦东机场。

• 一些旅客对浦东机场的未来改善持乐观态度，认为随着疫情缓解和科技手段的进一步应用，安检和海关的效率有望提升。

data.title: Mistaking Mary Magdalene
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了基督教中玛利亚·玛达肋纳（Mary Magdalene）的复杂形象及其历史争议。她是继耶稣母亲之后新约中最著名的女性，出现在四部福音书中，尤其在耶稣复活后扮演重要角色，被十三世纪神学家托马斯·阿奎那称为“使徒中的使徒”。然而，教会历史上对她的描绘充满矛盾：在东方正教会中她备受尊崇，而在西方教会中她既被视为圣人，也被描绘为罪人、妓女，甚至有人猜测她是耶稣的妻子。文章提到，新约中关于她的描述有限，且与其他多名同名玛丽混淆，导致其形象模糊不定。宗教学者伊莱恩·帕格斯（Elaine Pagels）指出，早期福音书中女性角色常被弱化，而《菲利普福音》等非正典文本则赋予玛达肋纳更大的影响力，视其为神圣智慧的体现。文章还讨论了玛达肋纳被误解为妓女的起源，指出这一形象源于公元591年教皇格里高利的布道，而非新约本身。最终，玛达肋纳成为一个充满神秘和矛盾的人物，象征着不确定性和边缘人群的守护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对评论内容的解读和可信性存在争议，特别是关于抹大拉的马利亚（Magdalene）相关历史和宗教叙述的解释。

不同观点：
• graemep认为原文中有很多推测和猜测的成分。虽然有些内容是公认的（如Gregory在声称马利亚是妓女中的角色），但这些信息在文中的解读值得怀疑。通常这些内容应被理解为耶稣对被传统标签为“坏”的人（如马太）的态度的体现。此外，graemep指出，某些内容非常荒谬，例如“耶稣可能在清理抹大拉的马利亚的脉轮”这一说法。

• gryfft提供了存档链接（https://archive.ph/lQqM9），但没有直接表达对原文内容的立场，可能是为了提供进一步的背景资料或让其他读者自行查阅相关讨论内容。

补充讨论：
• graemep对部分解读表示强烈怀疑，认为有些内容超出了合理的解释范围，尤其是那些涉及神秘主义或新时代（如“脉轮”）的内容。
• 争议的焦点集中在对抹大拉的马利亚历史角色和宗教地位的不同解读上。有些人试图用传统宗教视角解读，而另一些人引入了更具神秘色彩和新世纪信仰的解释，这导致了观点的冲突。
• graemep强调了历史和宗教叙述的传统解读与现代或非正统解读之间的张力，特别是在处理具有宗教和历史双重意义的人物时。

An ancient depiction of a naked woman hung on the wall of my father’s study. Skeletal, stupefied, and wildly bedheaded, she contemplated distances across time and space, as saints and mystics do. As with many of the unsettling religious tchotchkes scattered around the rectory where I spent my childhood, I didn’t give much thought to the unkempt icon, until more recently, when I grew curious about Mary Magdalene and began to read into the controversies swirling around her.
Magdalene is the most famous woman in Christianity after Jesus’ mother; she is also arguably the most hotly contested figure in the New Testament. A companion to Jesus in all four Gospels, she is present at his tomb, and, in some versions, is the first to see him after his Resurrection. In the Book of John, Jesus commissions her to share the good news of his return with the other disciples, which is why Thomas Aquinas, the thirteenth-century theologian, names her “the apostle to the apostles.” Nonetheless, Magdalene has been maligned by Church fathers throughout the centuries; in the present day, feminist scholars have championed her.
Magdalene, appearing in scripture only fourteen times, belongs to a tangle of at least six women named Mary. This multitude of Marys leaves considerable room for disagreement over which Biblical threads are authentically woven into Magdalene’s story, and which aren’t. In the Eastern Orthodox Church, she has a long and unassailed history of veneration. In the West, she’s been sanctified, but also portrayed as a sinner, a nun, a mystic, and Jesus’ wife. She remains, above all, a liminal figure. The patron saint of outcasts, she embodies uncertainty.
“There are so many disparate stories,”
Elaine Pagels
, the renowned religious scholar, told me on the sunporch of her home, in Princeton, New Jersey. To underscore the point, Pagels went to fetch a copy of “The New Oxford Annotated Bible,” flipping between the Books of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, and pausing over discrepancies between their Magdalene narratives. “The writers of the New Testament didn’t seem much interested in women except in their subsidiary roles,” she said. She poked around in the Book of Luke to show me how the author diminished Mary Magdalene’s significance. She’s present at the Resurrection, but only among other women. Instead of encountering the risen Lord, these women see two angels. “Luke deprecates her role,” Pagels said.
Pagel’s expertise, however, stretches far beyond the four Gospels that, by the start of the fifth century, had become the official canon. She has explored a much larger body of texts, many of which include women in more authoritative roles. Consider, she suggested, the Gospel of Philip—a third-century text discovered with similar documents near Nag Hammadi, in Egypt, in 1945—in which Magdalene is described as the woman “who always walked with the Lord” and “the one who was called his companion.” In its telling, her expansive influence transcends the terrestrial. As Pagels put it, “She’s seen as a manifestation of divine wisdom.”
Along with icons of anorexic saints, my childhood home was a place of books. Pagels’s “
The Gnostic Gospels
” shared a shelf with “
The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson
” and Carl Jung’s “
Memories, Dreams, Reflections
.” Each, in its own way, invited a friendly skepticism of orthodoxy and imbued value in people and ideas previously relegated to the edge. As Dickinson writes, “Tell all the truth but tell it slant.”
Mary Magdalene is a cipher for slantwise truth; to engage with her story requires divine imagination. Beyond the scant scriptural references, a rich treasury of myth can be found. My favorite, a thirteenth-century French narrative known as the Golden Legend, features Magdalene and Jesus’ friend Lazarus, who in this and some other accounts is said to be her brother. With a handful of followers, the two board a boat fourteen years after Jesus’ crucifixion and land on the southern coast of France. There, Magdalene lives and teaches until her death. Two duelling French monasteries still claim to hold her relics. On July 22nd, her feast day, they venerate her as their patron saint.
Magdalene is rendered more complex by associations with sexual desire: in the popular imagination, she’s a repentant prostitute. Yet, as I read more about who Mary Magdalene was, I was startled to learn that nothing in the New Testament associates her with licentiousness. Instead, this claim originated in a series of sermons given by Pope Gregory in 591. Gregory argued that Magdalene should be understood as highly sinful, referring to a story, in the Book of Luke, in which Jesus exorcised seven demons from her body. (Feminist scholars have questioned this interpretation, raising the possibility that Magdalene’s seven demons reflect the Eastern concept of seven chakras rather than a sinful nature. Maybe Jesus was clearing Magdalene’s chakras.)

data.article_summary: 《揭秘海怪》和《解释海洋传说》是亨利·李于1883年为国际渔业展览会撰写的两本小册子。该展览在伦敦举行，吸引了超过260万名参观者，其中最引人注目的是一个容纳65,000加仑水的大型水族馆。亨利·李是布莱顿水族馆的前博物学家，他通过理性分析和海洋研究的新发现，逐一解释并驳斥了诸如克拉肯和大海洋蛇等海怪传说。他认为这些 sightings 多为巨型鱿鱼等海洋生物的误认。在《解释海洋传说》中，他特别探讨了人鱼传说，认为这些多为海牛和儒艮的误认。李的作品既展示了海洋的神秘性，又体现了科学对海洋世界的探索，成为当时海洋神秘生物传说的重要记录。

Sea Monsters Unmasked
and
Sea Fables Explained
by Henry Lee (1883)
Henry Lee,
Sea Monsters Unmasked
(London: William Clowes and Sons, 1883).
Whether through their gleaming, glittering promotion of imagined (ever-improving) technological futures or their troubling “human zoo” displays of colonial peoples, a few World Fairs and Universal Expositions — the Great Exhibition of 1851 or Chicago World’s Fair of 1890 perhaps — have lived long in the imagination. Most, however, have not: the International Fisheries Exhibition of 1883 is among their number.
Between May and October of 1883, more than 2.6 million visitors travelled to see the spectacle in the grounds of the Royal Horticultural Society in London. At the centre of its displays from over thirty countries and colonies was an aquarium containing 65,000 gallons of water — the largest exhibition aquarium ever constructed. With an eye to posterity, the organisers did their best to promote themselves, creating a Literary Department that produced a variety of guides and handbooks for the exhibition throughout its six-month run. Two of these tie-in publications —
Sea Monsters Unmasked
and
Sea Fables Explained
— spoke particularly to the paradoxical place of the sea in both the imagination and science of the late nineteenth century: as a setting for tales of mysterious beasts, but also an increasingly scrutinised space for research on a shrinking globe.
Both books were written by Henry Lee (ca. 1826–1883), the former naturalist at the Brighton Aquarium and a prominent science communicator
du jour
. Numbering just over 100 pages each, Lee’s two brief works exude a Darwinian confidence. In them, a professional man of science, following in the great naturalist’s wake, exposes the follies of the past, rationalising traditional accounts through logical reasoning and recent discoveries in the marine world.
Although Lee narrates accounts of sea beasts to disprove them, the pamphlets also serve as unintended compendia of maritime folklore on aquatic cryptids. In
Sea Monsters Unmasked
, Lee focuses on the Kraken and the Great Sea Serpent. With the Kraken, he notes the regularity with which sightings emerged from Scandinavia and suggests that this helps explain why the Swedish taxonomist Carl Linnaeus included it in the first edition of his
System Naturae
. Of the many reports depicting the beast’s attacks on ships, Lee critiques Denys de Montfort’s account from 1680, known for its much-reproduced illustration, dismissing it as a “drawing fitter to decorate the outside of a showman's caravan at a fair than seriously to illustrate a work on natural history”. To Lee, thinking of the cuttlefish washed ashore and collected by European museums, the sightings of the Kraken were nothing more than encounters with squid, embellished for effect.
For the Great Sea Serpent, Lee lists sightings from Ancient Greece to the 1840s, spanning from the Mediterranean to North America — all observations of a giant snake-like creature. He also unpicks these accounts, arguing again that the most likely explanation for the sightings was the misidentification of giant squids. He highlights the washing ashore of a carcass on the Orcadian Island of Stronsay in 1808, which was claimed to be that of a sea serpent. Lee confidently asserts that “the whole fabric of circumstances” surrounding this claim “crumbled at the touch of science”. (It should be noted that before these claims were dismissed, the Natural History Society of Edinburgh believed there was sufficient evidence to declare the carcass to be that of a sea serpent.)
Henry Lee,
Sea Fables Explained
(London: William Clowes and Sons, 1883).
Lee’s second book,
Sea Fables Explained,
although featuring accounts of the Hydra and the Paper Nautilus, primarily focuses on sightings of mermaids. Lee takes — if you will — a deeper dive into encounters with this creature, not only drawing connections back to the belief systems of Mesopotamia but also documenting accounts from broader geographies than those of the other creatures he describes. Ultimately, Lee explains away mermaids, believing them to be sightings primarily of manatees and dugongs, whose wide global distribution accounted for the profundity of the tales.
For Lee, the accounts of sailors — “Jolly Jack Tars” — can be explained by the natural superstition he assumes sailors possess: “To the best of his belief, he has told the truth. He has seen some living being which looked wonderfully human, and his imagination, aided by an inherited superstition, has supplied the rest.” The imagination of one particular sailor quoted by Lee catches the eye of the twenty-first century reader, however; tucked away on page 74 of
Sea Monsters Unmasked

data.title: Agent Mesh for Enterprise Agents
data.author: pj3677
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了从大型主机到微服务的企业软件架构演变，强调当今企业需要能够自主推理、适应和行动的**代理系统（agentic systems）**。这种系统要求基础设施，尤其是网络，具有高度的动态性和语义理解能力，而传统网络无法满足这些需求。文章提出了一种新的网络架构概念——**代理网格（agent mesh）**，用于解决代理系统中的安全、可观测性、工具集成等问题。代理网格通过一个专用的**代理网关（agent gateway）**实现，支持代理与LLM（大语言模型）、工具及其他代理之间的安全通信和细粒度的访问控制，同时具备强大的可观测性和弹性保障。文章还讨论了代理与LLM的通信控制、工具集成以及多代理任务工作流的实现方式，旨在为企业提供一个统一的平台来管理和治理所有代理交互。

主要讨论点：Mesh代理与LLM后端的交互及相关技术术语的使用

不同观点：
• **tbrownaw** 认为，为了确保流量符合规则，Mesh代理需要调用LLM后端来处理自由形式的提示和生成内容。这表明在流量检查中，LLM后端的支持是必要的，以应对复杂的内容生成。

• **sdrg822** 对使用“Model Control Plane”这一术语持保留态度，认为在当前阶段就重复使用一个已流行的缩写为时尚早。这暗示了对新技术术语过早使用的担忧，可能导致混淆。

• **coldbrewed** 以一种讽刺的口吻将这个技术描述为“istio但带有AI生成的博客文章”，暗示这个新概念可能只是在已有技术上的小改进或包装，而非根本性的创新。

• **ActionHank** 对第七层的定义提出了疑问，质疑现在是否将代理之间的通信也视为第七层通信。这表明对传统网络层定义在现代技术背景下适用性的思考和质疑。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了对新技术术语使用的敏感性，以及对技术创新实际价值的质疑。
- 不同参与者对Mesh代理与LLM后端交互的必要性和实现方式有不同理解，部分人关注技术细节，而另一些人则关注更广泛的定义和分类问题。
- 争议的焦点在于新技术是否真正带来了创新，或者仅仅是已有技术的重新包装和术语重用。

43787493.article_content:
From mainframes to microservices, enterprises have evolved their software architectures to meet growing demands for scalability, flexibility, and adaptability. Todayâs reality demands more than just distribution or decomposition. In a world of real-time market shifts and ever-rising customer expectations, businesses need systems that can reason, adapt, and act on their own. This is the promise of
agentic systems
. This promise comes with a profound shift in what we expect from the infrastructure, especially the network.Â
Legacy networking was built around deterministic workflows â static APIs, predictable service calls and pre-defined paths. On the other hand, agentic systems are dynamic and emergent. They interpret user intent in natural language, orchestrate chains of agents and tools in real time, and make decisions on the fly. Security, observability, and routing is no longer just about headers or URLs, itâs about semantics and context. This shift demands a new kind of networking, one that supports intelligent adaptive policies at runtime, and provides observability across multi-hop workflows. We should future proof investments like this by supporting standard protocols. This new paradigm
needs an âagent meshâ
âa platform that enables security, observability, discovery, and governance across all agent interactions no matter where those agents, LLMs or tools are deployed. This post lays out that vision, and how we at Solo.io are ready to deliver this infrastructure.
An Agent Mesh
We believe enterprises building and deploying agentic systems will need to solve common security, observability, tenancy, and guardrail concerns. An
agent mesh
solves these challenges consistently for enterprise agent deployments (self-built, SaaS, developer tools like Cursor, etc) leveraging an
agent gateway
, a data plane tailored for these use cases.
An
agent mesh
consistently solves AI-specific networking challenges across three main interactions:
Agent to LLM communication
Agent to Tools / MCP
Agent to Agent / A2A
An
agent mesh
has the following properties:
Secure by default
: Agent identity, mTLS, and pluggable auth (OIDC, API keys, etc.)
Layer 7 native
: Supports agent-to-agent (A2A) and model control plane (MCP) communication
Fine-grained access control
: Authorization control for all agent and tool interactions
End-to-end observability
: Unified tracing across LLMs, agents, and tools
Registration and discovery
: Runtime agent/tool registration and lookup
Resilience and safety
: Guardrails, tool poisoning protection, and tenancy isolation
Modern ops model
: Declarative config and GitOps workflows
An
agent mesh
uses a specialized, highly performant data plane, an
agent gateway
, thatâs been tuned and optimized for AI communication patterns.Â
Letâs dig into the details of an
agent mesh
.Â
Controlling Agent to LLMÂ Communication
Agents often exchange sensitive prompts and payloads with an LLMâcustomer data, access tokens, internal documentsâand this traffic shouldnât go directly over the wire or bypass enterprise policies. Thatâs where an
agent gateway
must act as an âLLM gatewayâ. It can enforce policies such as guardrails, caching, and failover based on semantic understanding of the prompt. It can also do token-based rate limiting and usage tracking per user, tenant, or agent. Tracing what calls are sent to the LLM (and what responses were returned) is paramount. Tracking metrics like number of tokens consumed, guardrails tripped, and failovers detected is necessary to support enterprise observability.
â
â
An
agent gateway
can also make smart decisions for self-hosted inference backends (ie, AI models) backed by GPUs. It can use real-time telemetry to route prompts to the best available model taking into account metrics such as GPU KV cache, work queue depth, adapter deployment and criticality. The Inference Extension to Gateway API specifies an API for doing this.Â
Enabling Agents with Enterprise Tools
Agents individually cannot do interesting things without access to tools. Connecting LLMs to tools is a very open-ended problem which is recently solved with the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Describing tools, exposing them to agents, and allowing them to be invoked in a consistent manner (protocol) regardless of what the backing tool (database, API, file system, SaaS, etc) is addressed by MCP. Security, discovery, registration, tenancy and observability are left out of the protocol. 43787493.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了从大型主机到微服务的企业软件架构演变，强调当今企业需要能够自主推理、适应和行动的**代理系统（agentic systems）**。这种系统要求基础设施，尤其是网络，具有高度的动态性和语义理解能力，而传统网络无法满足这些需求。文章提出了一种新的网络架构概念——**代理网格（agent mesh）**，用于解决代理系统中的安全、可观测性、工具集成等问题。代理网格通过一个专用的**代理网关（agent gateway）**实现，支持代理与LLM（大语言模型）、工具及其他代理之间的安全通信和细粒度的访问控制，同时具备强大的可观测性和弹性保障。文章还讨论了代理与LLM的通信控制、工具集成以及多代理任务工作流的实现方式，旨在为企业提供一个统一的平台来管理和治理所有代理交互。

主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）与谷歌翻译在翻译质量上的对比，以及用户对自动翻译功能的接受度

不同观点：
• **itake的观点**：LLM在翻译质量上优于谷歌翻译，尤其是在长文本和需要额外上下文的场景下。itake提到谷歌翻译在处理用户生成内容（如Facebook帖子）时表现不佳，特别是在需要根据语境调整翻译的语言（如越南语中的称谓）时。他举例说明，与年长女性打招呼时，GPT能根据上下文提供更合适的翻译，而谷歌翻译则只能提供通用的翻译。

• **ttepasse的观点**：ttepasse对自动翻译功能持保留态度，尤其是当用户已经懂多种语言时。他认为，尽管机器翻译质量有所提高，但仍然存在“诡异谷”效应，即翻译内容虽然传达了信息，但感觉不自然。他以YouTube自动翻译视频标题和配音为例，抱怨缺乏让用户选择退出自动翻译的设置。

• **cj的观点**：cj对itake的免费/开源应用如何实现翻译功能表示好奇，特别是是否使用了Google Cloud Translate API。cj指出谷歌翻译API是付费服务，因此对itake如何实现应用的翻译功能表示疑问，猜测是否是用户自带API密钥（BYOK）的模式。

补充讨论：
• **翻译质量的比较**：itake通过具体例子展示了LLM在处理需要上下文的翻译时优于谷歌翻译，而ttepasse则从用户体验角度表达了对机器翻译不自然感的担忧。

• **自动翻译功能的用户选择**：ttepasse强调了用户应有选择退出自动翻译的自由，特别是在用户已经掌握多种语言的情况下，以避免不必要的翻译干扰。

• **技术实现的疑问**：cj对itake应用的技术实现方式表示疑问，特别是如何在免费/开源的情况下使用付费的翻译服务。

争议焦点：
• LLM与谷歌翻译在实际应用中的翻译质量和上下文处理能力。
• 用户是否应有选择退出自动翻译功能的自由，特别是在已经掌握多种语言的情况下。
• 免费/开源应用如何实现翻译功能的技术疑问。

data.title: People say they’ll pay more for “made in the USA” so we ran a test
data.author: ericzawo
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了一家公司为了测试消费者是否真的愿意为“美国制造”支付更高价格，进行了一项实验。他们将一款在亚洲生产的热销过滤花洒价格定为129美元，而相同设计的美国制造版本因成本高涨定价为239美元。结果显示，25,650名访问者中，没有一人购买美国制造版本，尽管其质量和设计完全相同。实验表明，尽管人们常说愿意支持美国制造，但在实际面临高价时，消费者往往选择更便宜的产品。作者指出，这不仅是他们公司的问题，而是整个经济面临的挑战，呼吁政策制定者关注这一现实问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：消费者是否愿意为“美国制造”的产品支付更高价格，以及影响这种选择的其他因素。

不同观点：
• **支持价格差异合理的观点**：一些评论认为，消费者愿意为“美国制造”的产品支付更多，但这个溢价应在合理范围内（如10-30%），而非85%的价差。他们指出，消费者可能更注重产品背后的故事、社区贡献以及道德或环保因素。([like_any_other], [gaiagraphia], [tejohnso])

• **质疑实验严谨性的观点**：有评论指出，文章缺乏足够的严谨性，数据不足，无法得出有意义的结论。实验应收集更多数据点，并考虑规模经济和成本因素，而不仅仅是比较价格差异。([hayst4ck], [pixelesque])

• **价格敏感性观点**：大部分消费者倾向于选择更便宜的产品，除非高价产品有显著的质量优势。消费者通常对价格敏感，尤其是在价差较大的情况下，不太可能为口号或标签支付更多。([pixelesque], [pif], [rietta])

• **对“美国制造”标签的信任问题**：一些评论质疑“美国制造”标签的真实性及其所暗示的质量。消费者可能因为怀疑标签的真实性或认为其不代表高质量而选择不支付更高价格。([JohnFen], [tejohnso], [mikewarot])

• **国际竞争与市场定价的讨论**：有评论指出，美国制造商面临国际竞争，特别是在低价市场部分，美国产品由于劳动力和环保合规成本更高，难以竞争。如果美国制造能回归并获得规模经济，价格可能会下降。([pfannkuchen], [devenson])

• **道德与消费选择的关系**：一些评论提到，消费者在感知影响较小或无人监督的情况下，往往会做出利己的消费选择，而不是基于道德或社会责任。([Workaccount2], [0xTJ])

补充讨论：
• 有评论建议通过动态调整价格来测试消费者对“美国制造”产品的实际支付意愿，而非简单比较两个固定价格。([oniony])

• 有评论提到特定产品领域（如水过滤）中，消费者更关注产品的功能和质量，而非产地标签。如果高价产品没有显著质量提升，消费者不会选择高价产品。([carterschonwald])

争议焦点：消费者是否真的愿意为“美国制造”支付显著更高的价格，以及这种溢价是否应与质量提升挂钩。实验设计的严谨性和“美国制造”标签的真实性也是争议的核心。

April 23, 2025
Share on Facebook
Share on twitter
Share on pintrest
When we priced a U.S.-made version of our flagship product 85% higher than our Chinese-made one, 25,650 customers had the chance to vote with their wallets. Here’s what happened.
As small business owners, we’ve heard it a thousand times:
“I’d gladly pay more to support American-made.”
We wanted to believe it. So we put it to the test.
We make filtered showerheads. Clean, sleek design. But more importantly, with the best shower filters on the market.
Our bestselling model—manufactured in Asia (China and Vietnam)—sells for $129. But this year, as tariffs jumped from 25% to 170%, we wondered: Could we reshore manufacturing to the U.S. while maintaining margins to keep our lights on?
An important part to mention is that our most filter materials (KDF-55) is sourced from the US. So technically we partly source from Asia.
We found a U.S.-based supplier. The new unit cost us nearly 3x more to produce. To maintain our margins, we’d have to sell it for $239.
So we ran an experiment.
We created a secret landing page. The product and design were identical. The only difference? One was labeled “Made in Asia” and priced at $129. The other, “Made in the USA,” at $239.
The visitors were given the choice to either buy the Made in USA or the Made in Asia version.
The results were sobering.
Add-to-carts for the U.S. version were only 24!
Conversion? 0.0% (zero).
Not a single customer purchased the Made-in-USA version.
We tested everything: color, copy, layout. We ran it over multiple days and traffic sources. Same outcome every time.
For a moment, we thought we’d made a technical error. We hadn’t.
This wasn’t a failure of marketing—it was a referendum on price.
We wanted to believe customers would back American labor with their dollars. But when faced with a real decision—not a survey or a comment section—they didn’t.
It’s not their fault. Most people are stretched. They’re feeling inflation everywhere: gas, groceries, mortgages. “Supporting U.S. manufacturing” becomes a luxury most can’t afford—even if they want to.
This isn’t just our problem—it’s the economy’s.
Small brands like ours want to manufacture here. We’re willing to invest. But without serious shifts—in consumer incentives, automation, and trade policy—the math doesn’t work. Not for us. Not for our customers.
We’re still committed to exploring local manufacturing. But for now, it’s not viable.
We’re sharing this because the numbers surprised even us. And we think they’re worth talking about.
If policymakers and pundits want to rebuild American industry, they need to grapple with this truth: idealism doesn’t always survive contact with a price tag.

data.title: Australian radio station using an AI-generated host
data.author: thedays
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚悉尼的CADA广播电台在未披露的情况下使用AI主持已有半年，且法律未要求披露。该AI主持名为“Thy”，每天播放四小时嘻哈音乐，其声音和形象来自ARN财务团队的一名员工。澳大利亚通信和媒体管理局表示，目前对广播中使用AI没有具体限制和披露义务。ARN称此举是探索新技术以提升听众体验，但也强调真实人物对内容的重要性。此事引发了对AI在媒体中应用的立法讨论，尤其在透明度和代表性方面。此前，其他电台也使用过AI主持，但均有披露。澳大利亚正在制定相关政策以确保AI的安全和负责任使用。

A Sydney radio station has been using an AI-generated host for about six months without disclosing it – and was not legally obliged to.
It was revealed last week that Australian Radio Network’s (ARN) Sydney-based CADA station, which broadcasts across western Sydney and is available online and through the iHeartRadio app, had created and deployed an AI host for its
Workdays with Thy
slot.
The artificial host known as “Thy” is on-air at 11am each weekday to present four hours of hip-hop, but at no point during the show, nor anywhere
on the ARN website
, is the use of AI disclosed.
CADA used an AI-generated host and didn’t disclose it. It didn’t have to.
Instead, the show’s webpage simply says “while you are at work, driving around, doing the commute on public transport or at uni, Thy will be playing you the hottest tracks from around the world”.
ARN Media also owns KIIS FM, the home of
The Kyle & Jackie O Show,
and the GOLD network, home to high-rating Sydney breakfast show
Jonesy & Amanda
.
After initial questioning from Stephanie Coombes in
The Carpet
newsletter, it was revealed that the station used ElevenLabs – a generative AI audio platform that transforms text into speech – to create Thy, whose likeness and voice were cloned from a real employee in the ARN finance team.
The Australian Communications and Media Authority said there were currently no specific restrictions on the use of AI in broadcast content, and no obligation to disclose its use.
A screenshot of the Workdays with Thy page of the CADA website.
An ARN spokesperson said the company was exploring how new technology could enhance the listener experience.
Advertisement
“We’ve been trialling AI audio tools on CADA, using the voice of Thy, an ARN team member. This is a space being explored by broadcasters globally, and the trial has offered valuable insights.”
Loading
However, it has also “reinforced the power of real personalities in driving compelling content”, the spokesperson added.
The Australian Financial Review
reported that
Workdays with Thy
has been broadcast on CADA since November, and was reported to have reached at least 72,000 people in last month’s ratings.
Vice president of the Australian Association of Voice Actors, Teresa Lim, said CADA’s failure to disclose its use of AI reinforces how necessary legislation around AI labelling has become.
“AI can be such a powerful and positive tool in broadcasting if there are correct safeguards in place,” she said. “Authenticity and truth are so important for broadcast media. The public deserves to know what the source is of what’s being broadcast … We need to have these discussions now before AI becomes so advanced that it’s too difficult to regulate.”
As an Asian woman working in Australian media, Lim said it also highlights how difficult it is for her demographic to break into broadcasting.
“When we found out she was just a cardboard cut-out, it cemented the disappointment. There are a limited number of Asian-Australian female presenters who are available for the job, so just give it to one of them. Don’t take that opportunity away from a minority group who’s already struggling.”
CADA isn’t the first radio station to use an AI-generated host. Two years ago, Australian digital radio company Disrupt Radio introduced its own AI newsreader, Debbie Disrupt. However, the fact that she wasn’t a real person was clearly disclosed from the beginning. And in 2023, an Oregon station in the US used an AI host, which was based on a real presenter.
An ACMA spokesperson said policies were still being developed in Australia to ensure safe and responsible use of AI. This is largely led by the Commonwealth Department of Industry, Science and Resources.
“This includes considering mandatory guardrails around transparency in high-risk settings, and the release of the
Voluntary AI Safety Standard
in September 2024.”

data.article_summary: OpenAlternative 是一个由社区驱动的开源项目，旨在提供专有软件和应用的开源替代品列表。该项目目标是成为用户寻找开源服务以支持业务增长的首选资源。它采用 GPL-3.0 许可证，依靠社区支持和赞助进行开发。项目使用 Turborepo 管理多包结构，采用 Bun 作为包管理器和运行时，并依赖多种第三方服务如 Neon 数据库和 Plausible 分析。开发者可以通过克隆项目、安装依赖、设置环境变量和运行开发服务器来贡献代码。项目最终可以部署在 Vercel 上。

About this project
OpenAlternative is a community driven list of
open source alternatives to proprietary software
and applications.
Our goal is to be your first stop when researching for a new open source service to help you grow your business. We will help you
find alternatives
of the products you already use.
Join us in creating the biggest
directory of open source software
.
Sponsoring
OpenAlternative is an GPL-3.0-licensed open source project with its ongoing development made possible entirely by the support of these awesome backers. If you'd like to join them, please consider
sponsoring OpenAlternative's development
.
If you'd like to support the project, you could also consider
buying our Next.js boilerplate
which is the foundation of creating directory websites, just like this one.
Services
OpenAlternative uses the following third-party services:
Database:
Neon
Analytics:
Plausible
,
PostHog
Newsletter:
Beehiiv
Background Jobs:
Inngest
File Storage:
AWS S3
Payments:
Stripe
Screenshots:
ScreenshotOne
Make sure to set up accounts with these services and add the necessary environment variables to your
.env
file.
Project Structure
OpenAlternative is built as a Turborepo monorepo with multiple packages. The project structure is organized as follows:
/apps
- Turborepo apps
/app
- Main Next.js application using the App Router architecture
/app
- Application routes and layouts (Next.js App Router)
/components
- Reusable React components
/lib
- Core utilities and business logic
/actions
- Server actions
/utils
- Helper functions and utilities
/hooks
- React hooks
/contexts
- React context providers
/services
- Service integrations
/emails
- Email templates
/server
- Server-side code
/functions
- Utility functions
/config
- Configuration files
/content
- Content management
/types
- TypeScript type definitions
/public
- Static assets
/analyzer
- Data analysis tools
/packages
- Shared packages
/db
- Database schema and utilities
/github
- GitHub integration utilities
The project uses Turborepo for task orchestration and dependency management across the monorepo.
Development
This project uses
Bun
as the package manager and runtime. Make sure you have Bun installed before proceeding.
To set up the project for development:
Clone the repository
Run
bun install
to install all dependencies
Set up the required environment variables (see below)
Run
bun run db:push
to push the Prisma schema to the database
Run
bun run dev
to start the application in development mode
Environment Variables
Refer to the
.env.example
file for a complete list of required variables.
Copy the
.env.example
file to
.env
and update the variables as needed:
cp .env.example .env
🧞 Commands
All commands are run from the root of the project, from a terminal:
Command
Action
bun install
Installs dependencies
bun run dev
Starts local dev server at
localhost:5173
bun run build
Build production application
bun run start
Preview production build locally
bun run lint
Run linter
bun run format
Format code
bun run typecheck
Run TypeScript type checking
bun run db:generate
Generate Prisma client
bun run db:studio
Start Prisma Studio
bun run db:push
Push Prisma schema to database
bun run db:pull
Pull Prisma schema from database
bun run db:reset
Reset Prisma schema
Deployment
The project is set up for deployment on Vercel. To deploy manually:
Build the project:
bun run build
Start the production server:
bun run start
Ensure all environment variables are properly set in your production environment.

data.title: Why I Blog and How I Automate it (2023)
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己为何写博客以及如何自动化这一过程。作者写博客主要是为了整理和深化自己从各种来源（如文章、视频）获得的知识，并通过撰写清晰的内容来验证自己的理解。作者使用一个基于Markdown的个人知识管理（PKM）系统，结合Obsidian和Zotero等工具，管理学习资料和笔记。作者从大量笔记中挑选出有价值的内容转化为博客文章，但希望将所有知识整合到一个系统中以方便搜索和链接。为实现这一目标，作者选择自己搭建静态网站，而不是使用如Substack等平台，以保持对网站外观和功能的完全控制。通过自动化发布流程，作者减少了发布和修改内容时的麻烦，从而更高效地分享知识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用Obsidian进行博客创作及内容自动化的讨论

不同观点：
• **[hxii的观点]**：  
  - 支持使用Obsidian进行博客创作，认为它提高了编辑的舒适度，并且能够在自己的资料库中方便地引用之前的文章。  
  - 分享了具体的实践经验，并提供了一个链接，进一步描述如何结合Obsidian和博客创作（https://0xff.nu/hajime-plus-obsidian）。

• **[ujkiolp的观点]**：  
  - 提出了一种层次化的内容创作理论：  
    - 创建内容是0级（实际创作）。  
    - 博客创作是-1级（讨论创作的过程）。  
    - 讨论博客创作是-2级（进一步讨论如何谈论创作的过程）。  
  - 隐含的批评是，讨论如何使用工具（如Obsidian）进行博客创作，可能是一种更为间接、低效的内容创作方式。

补充讨论：
• **对自动化的态度**：  
  - **[hxii]** 明显倾向于利用工具（如Obsidian）来提高创作效率和舒适度，显示出对自动化和工具辅助的支持。  
  - **[ujkiolp]** 则通过层次化的比喻，暗示过多的工具讨论可能偏离实际的内容创作，带有一定的批判性。

• **争议的焦点**：  
  - 讨论博客创作工具是否属于一种过于间接的、低效的创作方式。  
  - **[hxii]** 强调工具带来的实际好处，而 **[ujkiolp]** 则关注讨论工具本身是否偏离了直接的内容创作。

总结：  
讨论围绕使用Obsidian等工具进行博客创作的价值展开，一方强调其实际效益，另一方则关注这种讨论是否偏离了直接创作的核心。

Why I Blog and How I Automate it
2023-03-22
Pkm
Self hosting
Table of Contents
#
Why I Blog
I’m interested in consuming information in order to create new information (one of my motivations for pursuing a Ph.D.). I generally read articles/papers or watch videos, and then create papers/articles/code and have discussions as a result. While creating blog posts could be considered ‘giving back’, I think most of the benefit is personal because it (if well-written) forces me to make sense of and distill the ideas therein sufficiently such that someone else can understand me, which requires confronting various weaknesses and problems with the idea and improving on them (This is also one reason why I believe
feedback systems are important
).
Other sources refer to this as the
Knowledge Lifecycle
, of which I’ve included a screenshot below (the image comes from
A Complete Guide to Tagging for Personal Knowledge Management
(
link
) — they do a great job explaining this idea in detail which I won’t repeat).
My Markdown-based Personal Knowledge Management (
PKM
) notes system, which I’ve been building for years and currently interact with using
Obsidian
, is a grounds for this. In a nutshell, this is my process:
Organize how I ingest new knowledge. I usually learn from articles/blogs/papers/videos online and sometimes learn from books as well, but all of these, even finding out about said book, originate from a browser tab. I maintain different sets of browser tabs for different research areas in both work and personal pursuits and organize these using tools such as the awesome
BrainTool
and sometimes Obsidian. After writing this post, I created a
read-it-later solution
for this. ^85m76m
Any high-quality paper/article/video/etc. I read and want to remember goes into
Zotero
and synced between laptops/desktops via Syncthing (and is annotated there for PDFs only) (#todo write a post on link rot and my interest in preserving digital information)
Said annotations and links to the local
Zotero
file+URL are synced into Obsidian as a paired ‘Source’ note for whenever I want to write additional things regarding that source of information (via plugin
Obsidian-Zotero Integration
)
Non-Source notes in my PKM system are all my own writings and ideas which I often build off of Sources and their corresponding Source Notes using Markdown links and embeds (though sometimes I lazily skip this and just cite URLs)
A few of these notes become well-developed and useful (meaning useful even after they are written—I still think the act of writing itself forces the writer to clarify certain concepts and is useful even if the
writing itself
isn’t used again)
A few useful notes seem interesting enough that I think others may benefit from them, so I spend time improving the prose, generalizing them, etc., and create a blog post.
Out of 100 saved papers/articles, ~20 will have source notes, ~10 of those source notes lead to my own independent idea notes, ~4 of them become well-developed and useful, and just 1 gets turned into a blog post.
The problem with my previous site setup was that while all of my knowledge (from other sources or from me) was stored in my tightly-integrated Zotero+Obsidian setup (steps 1-4 above), step 5’s blog posts containing in principal my highest-quality technical assimilations of knowledge were disjointly stored in the site’s repository. I’d like to have everything in one place so it is all easily searchable and linkable and therefore give me greater opportunities to make new connections between my ideas and other sources’ ideas. Sure, I can just have multiple copies of the posts, but heaven forbid I have to correct that missed typo
in two places
. (Though in all seriousness, I wanted to eliminate any friction that would discourage me from publishing new content or improving existing posts.)
Thus, I wanted to find a way to better integrate all of my knowledge in one place and also seamlessly publish blog entries to increase the chances of me actually doing so. I may
stop using the term ‘blog’
in the future as I expect to update and improve these posts the same way I improve my own private notes (or ‘posts’).
#
How I Automate it
I often spend far too many hours building or automating things that have perfectly reasonable alternatives, because I find it fun to understand and control every step of the process (and on some rare occasions it becomes objectively useful as well). I’ve done this with my blog in my 2023 redesign—while I could have easily made an account on
https://substack.com/
, I prefer to have total control over the look and feel of the site (e.g., no annoying popups to subscribe after reading 1/4 down the article) and already had a simpler custom blog since 2019.
When I first acquired the domain ryanwwest.com, I had a Wordpress site for about a month and got very sick of it. I quickly decided instead to make a static site instead by just placing HTML/CSS/JavaScript files on my hosting server, but since I am

data.title: PgDog is a transaction pooler logical replication manager can shard PostgreSQL
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary: PgDog 是一个用于 PostgreSQL 的水平扩展解决方案，支持自动分片。它采用 Rust 编写，具有快速和安全的特点，能够管理数百个数据库和数十万个连接。PgDog 作为一个事务池和逻辑复制管理器，支持负载均衡、健康检查与故障转移、事务池管理以及自动查询路由和分片。它可以自动将查询路由到一个或多个分片，支持跨分片查询，并能在内存中组装结果。PgDog 还支持逻辑复制，允许在不停机情况下对数据库进行分片和扩展。其配置灵活，支持运行时调整，无需重启进程。可以通过 Docker 和 Kubernetes 快速部署。

PgDog is a transaction pooler and logical replication manager that can shard PostgreSQL. Written in Rust, PgDog is fast, secure and can manage hundreds of databases and hundreds of thousands of connections.
Documentation
📘 PgDog documentation can be
found here
. Any questions? Join our
Discord
.
Quick start
Kubernetes
Helm chart is
here
. To install it, run:
git clone https://github.com/pgdogdev/helm
&&
\
cd
helm
&&
\
helm install -f values.yaml pgdog ./
Docker
You can try PgDog quickly using Docker. Install
Docker Compose
and run:
docker-compose up
It will take a few minutes to build PgDog from source and launch the containers. Once started, you can connect to PgDog with psql (or any other PostgreSQL client):
PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U postgres
The demo comes with 3 shards and 2 sharded tables:

users (id, email)
VALUES
(
1
,
'
admin@acme.com
'
);
INSERT INTO
payments (id, user_id, amount)
VALUES
(
1
,
1
,
100
.
0
);
SELECT
*
FROM
users
WHERE
id
=
1
;
SELECT
*
FROM
payments
WHERE
user_id
=
1
;
Monitoring
PgDog exposes both the standard PgBouncer-style admin database and an OpenMetrics endpoint. The admin database isn't 100% compatible,
so we recommend you use OpenMetrics for monitoring. Example Datadog configuration and dashboard are
included
.
Features
Load balancer
PgDog is an application layer (OSI Level 7) load balancer for PostgreSQL. It can proxy multiple replicas (and primary) and distribute transactions evenly between databases. It supports multiple strategies, including round robin, random, least active connections, etc. PgDog can also inspect queries and send
SELECT
queries to replicas, and all others to the primary. This allows to proxy all databases behind a single PgDog deployment.
📘
Load balancer
Healthchecks and failover
PgDog maintains a real-time list of healthy hosts. When a host fails a healthcheck, it's removed from active rotation and queries are rerouted to other databases. This is similar to HTTP load balancing, except it's at the database layer.
Failover maximizes database availability and protects against bad network connections, temporary hardware failures or misconfiguration.
📘
Healthchecks
Transaction pooling
Like PgBouncer, PgDog supports transaction (and session) pooling, allowing
100,000s of clients to use just a few PostgreSQL server connections.
📘
Transactions
Sharding
PgDog is able to handle databases with multiple shards by routing queries automatically to one or more shards. Using the native PostgreSQL parser, PgDog understands queries, extracts sharding keys and determines the best routing strategy. For cross-shard queries, PgDog assembles results in memory and sends them all to the client transparently.
Using
COPY
PgDog comes with a CSV parser and can split COPY commands between all shards automatically. This allows clients to ingest data into sharded PostgreSQL without preprocessing.
Logical replication
PgDog understands the PostgreSQL logical replication protocol and can split data between databases in the background and without downtime. This allows to shard existing databases and add more shards to existing clusters in production, without impacting database operations.
📘
Sharding
Configuration
PgDog is highly configurable and many aspects of its operation can be tweaked at runtime, without having
to restart the process and break PostgreSQL connections. If you've used PgBouncer (or PgCat) before, the options
will be familiar. If not, they are documented with examples.
📘
Configuration
Running PgDog locally
Install the latest version of the Rust compiler from
rust-lang.org
.
Clone this repository and build the project in release mode:
cargo build --release
It's important to use the release profile if you're deploying to production or want to run
performance benchmarks.
Configuration
PgDog has two configuration files:
pgdog.toml
which contains general settings and PostgreSQL servers information
users.toml
for users and passwords

data.title: Microsoft subtracts C/C++ extension from VS Code forks
data.author: Dotnaught
data.article_summary: 微软从VS Code的衍生产品（如VS Codium和Cursor）中移除了C/C++扩展，导致开发者工作流受影响。该扩展提供了C/C++语言支持和调试功能，其移除限制了在非微软产品中使用，引发了开发者不满。自2020年9月起，微软的许可条款已规定其扩展仅限于自家产品使用，但直到2025年4月的更新才开始强制执行。Cursor通过设置反向代理绕过限制，但最新扩展已无法在其上运行。Cursor计划转向开源替代方案。与此同时，VS Codium用户在寻找自由和开源的替代品。有开发者向美国联邦贸易委员会投诉微软的不公平竞争行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕微软VS Code及其扩展市场的争议，以及对专有软件与开源软件的信任和依赖问题。

不同观点：
• **反对微软专有市场的观点**：一些用户（如bangaladore）认为微软的市场是专有的，虽然他们不喜欢这种模式，但更严重的是有公司为了自身利益公然违反使用条款，例如Cursor通过反向代理绕过微软的条款。这种行为被视为不道德的，尤其在依赖微软资源的情况下。

• **转向其他编辑器的观点**：kstrauser和yoyohello13等用户表示已经或准备转向其他编辑器，如Zed或不依赖微软的工具，因为他们不信任微软，并担心未来可能被“摆一道”。这种不信任尤其体现在对微软可能随时改变策略的担忧上。

• **技术替代方案的观点**：一些用户（如rs186、kentonv、elashri）讨论了技术上的替代方案，例如clangd在性能上优于微软的C++扩展。这些用户更倾向于使用开源解决方案，并认为开源社区可以填补微软专有软件留下的空白。

• **法律与商业策略的观点**：paxys和silverwind等用户认为，微软的行为虽然不理想，但也在意料之中，因为开源项目本身允许这样的操作。他们强调微软没有义务提供支持，用户如果依赖专有软件就应该预见到潜在的问题。

• **对开源与专有软件混合使用的反思**：concerndc1tizen提出了一种更广泛的社会现象，即很多人只关注自己的短期利益，忽视了更广泛的开源与专有软件混合使用可能带来的集体问题。这种反思引发了对个体选择和集体利益的讨论。

补充讨论：
• **编辑器和扩展的未来发展**：electroly和shmerl等用户讨论了Cursor等VSCode分支的未来，认为它们如果不转向微软的扩展生态系统，可能会面临生存问题。同时，其他编辑器（如Neovim和Sublime Text）也被提及作为替代方案。

争议的焦点：
• **是否应该依赖微软的工具和扩展**：一些用户认为依赖微软的工具不可避免地会导致问题，而另一些用户则认为可以通过开源解决方案来避免这些问题。

43788125.article_content:
Devops
6
Devs sound alarm after Microsoft subtracts C/C++ extension from VS Code forks
6
Cursor, Codium makers lose access as add-on goes exclusive
Thomas Claburn
Thu 24 Apr 2025
//
21:10 UTC
Microsoft's C/C++ extension for Visual Studio Code (VS Code) no longer works with derivative products such as VS Codium and Cursor – and some developers are crying foul.
In early April, programmers using VS Codium, an open-source fork of Microsoft's MIT-licensed
VS Code
, and Cursor, a commercial AI code assistant built from the VS Code codebase, noticed that the
C/C++ extension
stopped
working
.
The extension adds C/C++ language support, such as Intellisense code completion and debugging, to VS Code. The removal of these capabilities from competing tools breaks developer workflows, hobbles the editor, and arguably hinders competition.
The breaking change appears to have occurred with the release of v1.24.5 on April 3, 2025.
Following the April update, attempts to install the C/C++ extension outside of VS Code generate this error message: "The C/C++ extension may be used only with Microsoft Visual Studio, Visual Studio for Mac, Visual Studio Code, Azure DevOps, Team Foundation Server, and successor Microsoft products and services to develop and test your applications."
Microsoft has forbidden the use of its extensions outside of its own software products
since at least September 2020
, when the current licensing terms were published. But it hasn't enforced those terms in its C/C++ extension with
an environment check
in its binaries until now.
(Microsoft's PyLance extension for Python coding
is said
to have exhibited this behavior for years, preventing its use in VS Code forks.)
The latest releases of the specific extensions no longer work in Cursor or other non-MSFT editors
Michael Truell, co-founder and CEO of Anysphere, which makes Cursor, said in the discussion thread two weeks ago that a temporary fix has been rolled out and a more permanent solution is planned.
"MSFT has a handful of extensions which are closed-source," he
wrote
, pointing to Remote Access, Pylance, C/C++, and C#. "The latest releases of the specific extensions no longer work in Cursor or other non-MSFT editors.
"Moving forward, Cursor is transitioning away from these extensions. We are investing in open-source alternatives which already exist in the community and will bundle these into the next version to enable a seamless transition."
Cursor
allegedly
has been flouting Microsoft terms-of-service rules for some time now by setting up a reverse proxy to mask its network requests to the endpoints used by the Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace. This allows Cursor users to install VS Code extensions from Microsoft's market. Other VS Code forks tend to point to
Open VSX
, an alternative extension marketplace.
Truell did not respond to a request for comment.
As ChatGPT scores B- in engineering, professors scramble to update courses
Microsoft mystery folder fix might need a fix of its own
Ninite to win it: How to rebuild Windows without losing your mind
Microsoft 365 Copilot gets a new crew, including Researcher and Analyst bots
Meanwhile, users of VS Codium are
looking for
free (as in freedom) and open source alternatives.
Developers discussing the issue in Cursor's GitHub repo have noted that Microsoft
recently rolled out
a competing AI software agent capability,
dubbed Agent Mode
, within its Copilot software.
One such developer who contacted us anonymously told
The Register
they sent a letter about the situation to the US Federal Trade Commission, asking them to probe Microsoft for unfair competition - alleging self-preferencing, bundling Copilot without a removal option, and blocking rivals like Cursor to lock users into its AI ecosystem.
Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ®

data.title: The Urgency of Interpretability
data.author: jdkee
data.article_summary: 文章强调了解释人工智能（AI）系统内部运作的紧迫性，即“可解释性”。作者指出，尽管AI技术的发展不可阻挡，但我们仍能影响其发展方向和应用方式。当前AI系统的不透明性带来了风险，因为我们无法理解其决策过程，这可能导致意外的负面行为。可解释性可以帮助识别和预防这些问题，例如AI欺骗或权力寻求行为。然而，AI的发展速度快于可解释性的研究进展，因此需要加快后者的发展。作者呼吁业界共同努力，推动可解释性技术成熟，以确保AI安全和有益于社会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否已成为世界上最重要的经济和地缘政治问题

不同观点：
• 反对观点（aeve890）：认为AI并未成为最重要的经济和地缘政治问题。持这一观点的人表示无法认同AI已经达到如此重要的地位，暗示其言过其实。

• 支持观点（可能隐含在原文中）：认为AI已经从一个小众学术领域发展为对全球经济和地缘政治至关重要的问题。这一观点可能基于AI在各个行业中的广泛应用、对国家竞争力的影响以及其在国际关系中的战略意义。

补充讨论：
• 发展速度：有人提到AI在过去十年中快速发展，从学术研究走向实际应用，并逐渐影响全球事务。
• 争议焦点：主要在于AI的地位是否真的如某些人所说如此重要，这可能涉及对AI实际影响力和未来潜力的不同评估。
• 例子和论据：支持者可能引用AI在国防、经济、科技等领域的应用实例，如自动驾驶、智能制造、国家AI战略等，而反对者可能认为AI仍面临许多技术限制和社会挑战，其影响力被夸大。

The Urgency of Interpretability
April 2025
In the decade that I have been working on AI, Iâve watched it grow from a tiny academic field to arguably the most important economic and geopolitical issue in the world. Â In all that time, perhaps the most important lesson Iâve learned is this: the progress of the underlying technology is inexorable, driven by forces too powerful to stop, but the
way
in which it happensâthe order in which things are built, the applications we choose, and the details of how it is rolled out to societyâare eminently possible to change, and itâs possible to have great positive impact by doing so. Â We canât
stop
the bus, but we can
steer
it. Â In the past Iâve written about the importance of deploying AI in a way that is
positive for the world
, and of ensuring that democracies build and wield the technology
before autocracies do
. Â
Over the last few months, I have become increasingly focused on an additional opportunity for steering the bus: the tantalizing possibility, opened up by some recent advances, that we could succeed at
interpretability
âthat is, in understanding the inner workings of AI systemsâ
before
models reach an overwhelming level of power.
People outside the field are often surprised and alarmed to learn that we do not understand how our own AI creations work. Â They are right to be concerned: this lack of understanding is essentially unprecedented in the history of technology. Â For several years, we (both Anthropic and the field at large) have been trying to solve this problem, to create the analogue of a highly precise and accurate MRI that would fully reveal the inner workings of an AI model. Â This goal has often felt very distant, but multiple
recent
breakthroughs
have convinced me that we are now on the right track and have a real chance of success.
At the same time, the field of AI as a whole is further ahead than our efforts at interpretability, and is itself advancing very quickly. Â We therefore must move fast if we want interpretability to mature in time to matter. Â This post makes the case for interpretability: what it is, why AI will go better if we have it, and what all of us can do to help it win the race.
The Dangers of Ignorance
Modern generative AI systems are opaque in a way that fundamentally differs from traditional software. Â If an ordinary software program does somethingâfor example, a character in a video game says a line of dialogue, or my food delivery app allows me to tip my driverâit does those things because a human specifically programmed them in. Â Generative AI is
not like that at all
. Â When a generative AI system does something, like summarize a financial document, we have no idea, at a specific or precise level, why it makes the choices it doesâwhy it chooses certain words over others, or why it occasionally makes a mistake despite usually being accurate. Â As my friend and co-founder Chris Olah is
fond of saying
, generative AI systems are
grown
more than they are
built
âtheir internal mechanisms are âemergentâ rather than directly designed. Â Itâs a bit like growing a plant or a bacterial colony: we set the high-level conditions that direct and shape growth
1
, but the exact structure which emerges is unpredictable and difficult to understand or explain. Â Looking inside these systems, what we see are vast matrices of billions of numbers. Â These are
somehow
computing important cognitive tasks, but exactly how they do so isnât obvious.
Many of the risks and worries associated with generative AI are ultimately consequences of this opacity, and would be much easier to address if the models were interpretable.
For example, AI researchers often worry about misaligned systems that could take harmful actions not intended by their creators. Â Our inability to understand modelsâ internal mechanisms means that we cannot meaningfully predict such behaviors, and therefore struggle to rule them out; indeed, models
do
exhibit unexpected emergent behaviors, though none that have yet risen to major levels of concern. Â More subtly, the same opacity makes it hard to find definitive evidence
supporting
the existence of these risks at a large scale, making it hard to rally support for addressing themâand indeed, hard to know for sure how dangerous they are.
To address the severity of these alignment risks, we will have to see inside AI models much more clearly than we can today. For example, one major concern is AI deception or power-seeking. Â The nature of AI training makes it possible that AI systems will develop, on their own, an ability to deceive humans and an inclination to seek power in a way that ordinary deterministic software never will; this emergent nature also makes it difficult to detect and mitigate such developments
2

data.title: Show HN: We made a blazing-fast, open-source GitHub front end
data.author: Arian81
data.article_summary: Gitfaster 是一个极速、简洁的 GitHub 客户端，旨在提升使用体验，避免传统软件的迟缓感。其主要功能包括：自动预取文件以加速浏览，缓存 GitHub API 的慢响应以快速访问，以及整体设计注重性能表现，既快又流畅。该工具专为追求高效的开发者设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对代码托管平台及前端界面的功能与改进建议

不同观点：
• [philocalyst] 对项目表示赞赏，并提出功能改进建议。具体包括：希望显示仓库的更多信息（如语言分类、标签等），以及考虑在侧边栏中增加更多功能，例如星图或代码行数统计图表。此外，philocalyst 提到了一个类似的平台 "Gothub"，并建议项目团队可以参考其他替代前端界面的列表，如果认真考虑这个方向，还可以提供易于理解的自托管说明。

• [Arian81] 提供了一个具体的替代方案，提到用户可以通过访问 "gitfaster" 平台查看源代码，并给出了相关链接。同时，Arian81 还介绍了一个小技巧：将 GitHub 链接中的 "github" 改为 "githubf" 即可通过他们的应用查看代码。

• [nguyenkien] 对项目网站的登录要求提出疑问，表示如果需要登录，那还不如直接使用 GitHub.dev，暗示 GitHub.dev 已经能满足其需求，因此对新平台的必要性提出隐含质疑。

补充讨论：
• philocalyst 对项目功能扩展表现出积极兴趣，并提到了其他替代前端，建议项目可以更加开放和易用。
• Arian81 专注于提供一个直接的替代工具（gitfaster），并引导用户使用该平台。
• nguyenkien 则关注实用性，尤其是登录要求是否会增加用户的使用成本，并对项目是否能比 GitHub.dev 提供更多价值提出质疑。

争议焦点：项目的独特价值与用户使用的便捷性。philocalyst 希望项目能扩展功能以区别于其他平台，而 nguyenkien 则质疑项目是否必要，尤其在需要登录的情况下。

data.title: mruby 3.4.0
data.author: shaicoleman
data.article_summary: mruby 3.4.0 发布了首个稳定版本，引入多项新特性与更改。主要变化包括支持 `private` 和 `protected` 方法可见性，减少内联符号最大长度，优化二进制字符串处理，改进数组排序和字符串操作等。C API 也有多项调整，如重命名文件和函数以减少混淆。新增多个构建目标和平台支持，如 Playstation Portable 和 Emscripten。mrbgems 方面，移除了 `mruby-print`，并为 `mruby-enum-lazy`、`mruby-io` 等添加新功能。此外，修复了多个 GitHub 问题，提升了编译和运行时的稳定性和性能。详细的变更日志可参阅 `doc/mruby3.4.md` 文件。

data.title: Yahoo Wants to Buy Chrome
data.author: pier25
data.article_summary: Yahoo正在开发自己的网页浏览器原型，并表示如果法院要求谷歌出售Chrome，它有意收购。美国司法部正在寻求解决谷歌搜索垄断问题，其中包括要求谷歌出售Chrome浏览器。不仅是Yahoo，DuckDuckGo、Perplexity和OpenAI等公司也对Chrome表示了兴趣。Yahoo认为拥有浏览器对搜索业务至关重要，目前正在内部开发浏览器原型，预计需六到九个月。收购Chrome将更快提升其市场份额，预计可从目前的3%增至两位数。Yahoo估计收购费用需数百亿美元，并表示其所有者Apollo Global Management可以提供资金支持。Apollo还拥有曾在另一反垄断案中成为焦点的浏览器品牌Netscape。

不同观点：
• 一方对Yahoo的现状表示疑问，特别是对其目前的业务和财务状况感到不解（KeplerBoy）。具体来说，质疑Yahoo作为一个仍在支付数千名员工工资的公司，究竟在从事哪些业务活动，尤其是因为Yahoo的许多消费者服务（如其金融应用）看似没有显著增长或创新。

• 另一方（潜在回应者，虽然在评论中未直接出现）可能会指出，Yahoo尽管在消费者心目中的存在感下降，但实际上通过多种业务途径维持运营，包括广告收入、与Verizon的合作以及其在媒体和科技领域的投资。

补充讨论：
• Yahoo的主要收入来源可能包括其广告业务，尤其是通过其新闻平台和媒体内容所带来的流量变现。此外，Yahoo在2017年被Verizon收购后，成为其子公司Oath（后更名为Verizon Media）的一部分，这可能是其维持运营的一个重要因素。

• 有人可能会提到Yahoo在技术和服务上的创新不足，导致其在消费者市场的影响力下降，但其B2B业务和合作伙伴关系可能仍在支撑公司运转。

• 争议焦点可能在于Yahoo能否在当前竞争激烈的科技和媒体行业中找到新的增长点，以维持其长期生存和发展。

43787857.article_content:
Policy
Yahoo wants to buy Chrome
And it’s prototyping its own web browser.
And it’s prototyping its own web browser.
by
Lauren Feiner
Apr 24, 2025, 9:24 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: The Verge
Lauren Feiner
is a senior policy reporter at The Verge, covering the intersection of Silicon Valley and Capitol Hill. She spent 5 years covering tech policy at CNBC, writing about antitrust, privacy, and content moderation reform.
Legacy search brand Yahoo has been working on its own web browser prototype, and says it would like to buy Google’s Chrome if the company is forced by a court to sell it.
The information came out during the fourth day of the Justice Department’s remedies trial to rectify Google’s search monopoly. The DOJ has — among other proposals — requested Judge Amit Mehta break up Google by
requiring it sell its Chrome browser
, which the agency says is a key distribution channel for its popular search engine that’s amassed too much power for anyone else to compete. Yahoo isn’t the only company interested in buying Chrome. While DuckDuckGo’s CEO said they wouldn’t be able to afford it,
witnesses from Perplexity and OpenAI
both expressed interest in the popular browser on the stand this week.
Witnesses from Perplexity and OpenAI both expressed interest in Chrome
Yahoo seems to agree that owning a web browser is a very important portal for search, and is looking to run its own, either through developing or buying one. Yahoo Search General Manager Brian Provost testified that about 60% of search queries are done through a web browser; many people search directly from the address bar. That’s why, Provost testified, since last summer Yahoo has been “actively internally developing a prototype of a browser” to understand what it would need to do to put one out in the market. He added that Yahoo is in “ongoing” discussions with other companies about buying a browser, though he would not publicly state which ones it’s in talks with.
For Yahoo, prototyping its own browser will take six to nine months, Provost estimated. Acquiring Chrome would likely be a much faster way to ramp up to scale. Provost called Chrome “arguably the most important strategic player on the web,” and estimated Yahoo’s search market share could jump from 3 percent to double digits if it were able to buy the browser. He estimated the deal would cost tens of billions of dollars, and said Yahoo would be able to secure that funding with the backing of its owner, Apollo Global Management. Apollo actually owns a browser brand that was at the center of a different antitrust case, but Provost said he wouldn’t consider it an active browser. The brand’s name?
NetScape

• [phony-account] 认为字体许可费用在移动应用开发领域过高，尤其是与印刷领域相比。他认为如果许可更合理，盗版问题可能会减少。
• [rglover] 表示愿意为价格合理的字体付费，比如单个字重$5-$10，整个字体家族$20-$100，但他认为目前许多字体的定价过高，因此选择使用Google Fonts等免费或更便宜的替代品。
• [mchusma] 认为字体设计本身不应受版权保护，因为字体是基于公共领域的微小变化，且大多数人无法区分。他建议如果字体有技术改进，应通过专利保护。
• [jll29] 感到悲哀的是，许多人没有意识到设计字体需要大量的创造力、工艺和时间，他们不尊重字体设计的价值。
• [efitz] 提到LLM（大型语言模型）和SVG技术的结合可能导致未来无需许可即可使用类似字体，这将对现有的字体商业模式造成冲击。
• [tossandthrow] 认为版权道德基础正在崩溃，变成一种大家认为可笑且不执行的法律，令人遗憾。

补充讨论：
• [azalemeth] 提到一个反讽的例子，指出反盗版广告本身可能使用了侵权字体。
• [mrkeen] 补充了反盗版广告还盗用了音乐。
• [jchw] 讨论了字体版权和历史关联，如XBAND peripheral与某字体的潜在关系，但未找到确凿证据。
• [socalgal2] 了解到在美国字体设计本身不受版权保护，但字体文件受保护，并提出在实践中如何区分复制与灵感借鉴的问题。
• [ummonk] 强调只要不直接复制字体文件的代码，视觉上模仿字体设计是合法的。
• [pelagic_sky] 分享了作为设计师的教育和工作经历，强调在专业环境中购买和许可字体的重要性。
• [ks2048] 查找了反盗版广告活动的背景信息，指出其与FACT和MPAA的关联。

争议焦点：
• 字体许可费用的合理性，尤其是在不同使用场景（如印刷 vs. 移动应用开发）下的差异。
• 字体设计是否应受版权保护，以及如何在法律和实践中区分版权侵权和合法借鉴。
• 未来技术（如LLM）可能对字体设计和版权保护带来的冲击。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术进步是否能够解决人类重大问题，以及对未来科技乌托邦的争议。

不同观点：
• aeturnum认为，“技术拯救未来”是一种低信息量的逃避现实的想法，类似于宗教信仰。他指出，虽然技术有潜力，但我们无法仅依靠技术解决气候变化等重大问题。那些鼓吹技术万能的人往往是为了从中获利，而非真正解决问题。
• golol反对aeturnum的观点，认为技术是实现实质性改进的唯一途径。他批评了对科技企业家的贬低，并指出政治上的资源分配无法真正改善世界。
• blaze33也质疑“技术万能”的理念，认为这种思维暗示了当前所有问题都不需要反思，且忽视了人类活动对危机的责任。他希望看到的是一个在地球上和平共处的未来，而不是因为地球环境恶化而被迫移民火星。
• schnitzelstoat支持技术进步的希望，认为如果没有技术进步和经济增长，世界将变得零和。他指出，技术进步虽然可能过于乐观，但总比停滞和历史上的大规模人类苦难要好。
• iNic承认技术对自然的改造能力，但对短期内建立火星殖民地持怀疑态度。他更关注AI的颠覆性影响。
• janalsncm批评了一些科技名人对自己不熟悉领域的夸夸其谈，认为他们不应被赋予过多的发言权。
• nektro幽默地提出，能否通过技术发明来消除亿万富翁，因为他们是许多问题背后的共同因素。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了TESCREAL（超人类主义、Extropianism、奇点主义、现代宇宙主义、理性主义、有效利他主义和长期主义）这一思想束，与现代硅谷科技圈的关联，并追溯到18世纪的思想家如Nikolai Fyodorov。
• 有人提到乐观的科幻作品如Culture系列，认为这类作品能够改变人的思维方式。
• 讨论中还涉及对内容审核和平台过滤的质疑，以及对某些讨论被删除或降权的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于技术是否能够独自解决人类重大问题，如气候变化和不平等。一方认为技术是万能的解决方案，另一方则认为这种想法是逃避现实，且可能被用作牟利工具。
• 对科技企业家和名人在技术话题上的发言权和可信度的质疑，也是讨论中的一个重要分歧点。

该仓库（msfroh/lucene-university）提供了自包含的Apache Lucene功能示例代码，并附有详细的代码注释（Markdown格式），旨在帮助用户理解Lucene的各种特性。主要包括：

1. 示例代码可通过阅读源码或使用IDE调试来学习，并支持在网页上浏览（使用Docco生成）。
2. 依赖Lucene 10和JDK 21及以上版本，通过Gradle构建。
3. 贡献指南要求每个示例自包含，仅导入Lucene和Java类，且每个示例类需包含`main`方法和注释说明。
4. 代码基于Apache-2.0许可证发布。

用户可通过克隆仓库并导入IDE来运行和修改示例。
