43777478.article_content:
Contra Thomas Wolfe, you actually
can
go home again—but once you see how much it’s changed, you may want to leave just as quickly. When Henry James, after spending most of his adult life abroad, returned in 1904 for a 10-month-long tour of the United States, he was dismayed to find that many of the old buildings and spaces he once cherished had been obliterated—such as his childhood homes in Boston and Manhattan’s Washington Square or the “dusky lecture halls” of Copley Square, where his father (a theosophy-leaning lover of Swedenborg) had once given talks, along with the likes of Ralph Waldo Emerson and the abolitionist Wendell Phillips. Even worse: In their places had risen implacable monuments and skyscrapers that stood unassailable to James’s nightly flaneur-ish ramblings; they no longer reverberated with his fading memories of youth but only testified to America’s “power of the purse.”
The U.S. had become a largely unfamiliar country filled with strange new architectures and foreign voices. And while James had hoped to rediscover his homeland with freshly scrubbed perceptions (much as, when a young man, he first discovered his love for Italy, France, and London), he soon found himself just as “lost in America” as Albert Brooks would a century later. “The very sign of its energy,” he went on to write in his late, impressive, and often complexly difficult travel memoir,
The American Scene,
in 1907:
is that it doesn’t believe in itself: it fails to succeed, even at a cost of millions, in persuading you that it does. Its mission would appear to be, exactly, to gild the temporary, with its gold, as many inches thick as may be, and then, with a fresh shrug, a shrug of its splendid cynicism for its freshly detected inability to convince, give up its actual work, however exorbitant, as the merest of stop-gaps. The difficulty with the compromised charmer is just this constant inability to convince; to convince ever, I mean, that she is serious, serious about any form whatever, or about anything but that perpetual passionate pecuniary purpose which plays with all forms, which derides and devours them, though it may pile up the cost of them in order to rest a while, spent and haggard, in the illusion of their finality.
Henry James Comes Home: Rediscovering America in the Gilded Age
By Peter Brooks
Buy on Bookshop
New York Review Books, 248 pp., $18.95
It’s the sort of convoluted passage that runs throughout
The A
merican Scene
,
often taking as much time for a reader to unravel as James spent raveling it. Basically, James argues that early twentieth-century America liked to “gild” things just long enough to fool observers into believing they were worth gilding; but as soon as this illusion fades away or wears off, America quickly moves on to purveying the next one.
Everywhere James looked, he saw money motivating people away from the cultural pleasures and beauties that he loved (theaters, libraries, and art galleries). It is hard to think of an American writer who was more disgusted with the dirty realities of capitalism, or one who worked so hard to make money doing the brighter, cleaner things he loved—composing books, stories, plays, and essays.
Henry
James Comes Home
arrives as a late companion piece to preeminent Jamesian scholar Peter Brooks’s earlier, similarly structured book,
Henry James Goes to Paris
(2007), which described James’s youthful engagements with Turgenev, Zola, Sand, and Flaubert—during which he learned, or saved away to adopt later in life, those “modern” fictional techniques that distinguished French novelists in the latter half of the nineteenth century. Along the way, Brooks examined how these techniques came to be used in James’s greatest novels, such as
The Ambassadors
and
The Wings of the Dove
. In these works, Brooks wrote, “James appears to reach back to lessons learned in Paris in the mid-1870s—to the lessons of Flaubert, but also more generally to what he picked up in the city that was inventing modernism. It’s as if what James rejected in 1875–76 had lain dormant in him ever since, only coming to flower at the
fin de si
è
cle.
”
Brooks’s two “mini-biographies” of James, each covering only a few years in the writer’s long and productive life, seek to uncover the “international” qualities of a man who may be America’s first truly “international” writer. Brooks’s first book of criticism,
The Novel of Worldliness:
Crebillon, Marivaux, Laclos, Stendhal
(1969), examined the ways literature developed from, and influenced, a cultural world that extended across nations and continents; and it significantly arrived at a time when many of the so-called “New Critics” (and later, Brooks’s Yale “deconstructionist” colleagues, such as De Man, Miller, and Derrida) usually focused on the microscopic, apolitical, and even ahistorical features of individual stories, novels, and poems. Against the tide of his contemporaries, Brooks has preferred to read across the lifetimes of individual authors and

data.title: A Visual Journey Through Async Rust
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了通过可视化方式理解Rust中的异步执行。作者创建了一个程序，通过计算正弦函数的值并使用`matplotlib`和`pyo3`绘制出结果，来观察异步任务的执行顺序和并发情况。程序中，多个异步任务交替执行，并通过通道发送计算结果。为了更清晰地展示每个任务的执行时间，作者在样本中加入了计算开始和结束的时间戳，并通过图形化显示这些时间。

文章还解释了并发和并行的区别：并发是任务交替执行，而并行则是任务同时执行。最后，作者通过引入更耗时的CPU操作（如`sin_high_cpu`），展示了CPU密集型任务如何阻塞异步执行器，并影响其他异步操作的执行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的异步编程及其相关问题，包括CPU密集型任务、阻塞I/O操作、以及与其他语言/平台的比较。

不同观点：
• OskarS：认为CPU密集型任务必然会占用CPU资源，但可以通过将任务拆分为小块并使用`.await`或后台线程来缓解。更严重的问题是阻塞I/O操作，它不仅占用CPU，还阻碍事件循环，导致资源利用率低下。如果选择异步I/O，所有I/O操作都需要是异步的，否则会丧失异步的优势。

• Inglor：指出Node.js中可以使用`worker_threads`或者类似Tokio的API（如Piscina）来实现任务 spawn 和 futures 运行。同时提到Rayon在处理CPU密集型任务时表现良好，可以与Tokio混合使用，尽管有一些注意事项。

• Vermilingua：提出文章中未提及的一个问题，即在spawned线程上运行的计算生成的正弦波曲线有变形，质疑这是绘图问题还是Tokio线程时间跟踪不准确。

• Jdnier：以幽默方式评论生成的正弦波像多声部音乐谱，并提到可能受其他运行进程影响的音高变化。

• Binary132：希望看到类似的跨多个运行时的比较，而不仅限于Rust。

• Rc00：只是分享了一个相关的Hacker News链接，未发表具体观点。

• Jwufasdfsds：提到可以通过使用Plan9或Inferno来避免异步灾难，但并不作为对async-rust的批评，认为在Linux等传统平台上仍需使用异步Rust。

• ModernMech：对“drop pennies”这一表达感到困惑，询问其含义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了Rust异步编程中的实际问题，如阻塞I/O和CPU密集型任务的处理，以及与其他语言和平台（如Node.js）的比较。
• 有人提到具体工具和库（如Rayon和Piscina）的实际应用经验，提供了对异步和多线程编程的具体解决方案和建议。
• 对文章中未提及的技术细节（如正弦波变形问题）进行了补充讨论，提出了可能的技术问题或误解。
• 最后，有人对英语习语“drop pennies”的含义感到困惑，显示出对技术文章中文化表达的理解差异。

文章介绍了通过可视化方式理解Rust中的异步执行。作者创建了一个程序，通过计算正弦函数的值并使用`matplotlib`和`pyo3`绘制出结果，来观察异步任务的执行顺序和并发情况。程序中，多个异步任务交替执行，并通过通道发送计算结果。为了更清晰地展示每个任务的执行时间，作者在样本中加入了计算开始和结束的时间戳，并通过图形化显示这些时间。

文章还解释了并发和并行的区别：并发是任务交替执行，而并行则是任务同时执行。最后，作者通过引入更耗时的CPU操作（如`sin_high_cpu`），展示了CPU密集型任务如何阻塞异步执行器，并影响其他异步操作的执行。

不同观点：
• OskarS：认为CPU密集型任务必然会占用CPU资源，但可以通过将任务拆分为小块并使用`.await`或后台线程来缓解。更严重的问题是阻塞I/O操作，它不仅占用CPU，还阻碍事件循环，导致资源利用率低下。如果选择异步I/O，所有I/O操作都需要是异步的，否则会丧失异步的优势。

data.author: alexboehm
data.article_summary: Faasta 是一个高效的函数即服务（FaaS）平台，具有极快的速度和低内存开销。它通过 WebAssembly 架构实现，冷启动时间低于 1 毫秒，内存开销小于 1KB。主要特性包括：基于 WASI P2 和 WASIHTTP 标准运行 WebAssembly 模块，确保安全隔离和高效的 HTTP 请求处理；超快的冷启动速度；支持自托管；代码可移植性强。使用步骤包括安装 Faasta CLI、创建项目、构建和部署函数。平台目前处于实验阶段，可能会有重大变化。Faasta 提供免费托管实例，用户也可以自行部署。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕项目 "Faasta" 的不同方面的讨论，包括与竞争项目 Bun 的比较、技术实现细节、名称冲突问题、开源许可和功能扩展的可能性。

不同观点：
• [kaliqt] 认为 Faasta 项目可能会与 Bun 项目形成竞争，Bun 也是一个强调紧凑和速度的项目，且速度是 Bun 的主要优先项。kaliqt 提出 Faasta 需要思考如何在成长过程中与 Bun 形成差异化。

• [xkcd-sucks] 指出 "Faasta" 的名称与生物信息学中的 FASTA 序列文件格式有冲突，可能会引起混淆。

• [mrmagoo17] 对 Faasta 的实现表示赞赏，并期待研究其代码。同时对主要云供应商尚未考虑利用 WASM 和 WASI 技术进行无服务器计算表示惊讶。

• [singularity2001] 建议在 GitHub 中添加链接到 faasta.xyz 并在关于页面和示例中进行说明，提出 lambdas 应该能够通过 http(s) 访问，并给出具体路径示例，认为如果实现得当，这将是一个好主意。

• [foresterre] 关注项目的开源许可问题，指出在仓库中没有看到 LICENSE 文件，并询问该项目是否会是开源项目，或者是否有开放核心或类似的许可模式。

• [badmonster] 关心自托管部署的功能，询问是否会支持自定义域名和 SSL 证书，或者这些功能是否需要通过外部反向代理来处理。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前没有直接的争议，但 [kaliqt] 提到了 Faasta 和 Bun 之间的潜在竞争关系，暗示 Faasta 需要找到自己的独特定位。

这些讨论点反映了社区对 Faasta 项目的关注和期望，涵盖了技术、命名、许可和功能等多个方面。

Faasta: a Faster FaaS Platform
Faasta is a cutting-edge Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platform designed for exceptional speed and efficiency. With
cold start times under 1ms
and a
memory overhead of less than 1KB
, Faasta delivers unparalleled performance through its modern WebAssembly architecture.
Key Features
Runs your code as
WebAssembly modules
using the WASI P2 standard
Leverages
WASIHTTP
for high-performance HTTP request handling
Provides
secure isolation
between functions through WebAssembly's sandboxed execution model
Achieves
ultra-fast cold starts
without the overhead of traditional containerization
Self-hostable
with simple setup - run your own Faasta instance anywhere
Standards-compliant
with WASI P2 and WASIHTTP, making your functions portable
Powered by
Wasmtime
for efficient WebAssembly execution
Includes a
free hosted instance
at
faasta.xyz
Your code is compiled to WebAssembly with
strict safety requirements
, ensuring:
🔒 Secure execution within the WebAssembly sandbox
✅ Whitelisted dependencies
🌐 Standards-compliant implementation using WASI P2 and WASIHTTP
Getting Started
Install the Faasta CLI:
cargo install cargo-faasta
Create a new Faasta project:
cargo faasta init
#
or
cargo faasta new my-function
Build your function for WebAssembly:
cargo faasta build
Login with your GitHub account:
cargo faasta login
Deploy your function:
cargo faasta deploy
Your function will be available at
https://your-function-name.faasta.xyz
WASI P2 and WASIHTTP
Faasta implements the WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) Preview 2 specification and the WASIHTTP standard to enable:
Standardized HTTP request and response handling
Component-based architecture for better modularity
Consistent interface for interacting with the host system
Portable functions that can run on any WASI P2 compatible runtime
Because Faasta uses these open standards, your functions are not locked to a specific platform and can be hosted anywhere that supports these standards.
Self-Hosting
Faasta is fully self-hostable. You can run your own instance of the Faasta server to host your functions on your own infrastructure.
⚠️
Experimental Status
Faasta is currently experimental. There will be breaking changes that will interupt service on the faasta.xyz instance.

文章描述了作者在巴西一片奇特的尤加利树林边缘遭遇汽车抛锚的经历。这些尤加利树生长得整齐划一，树干高耸，顶部枝叶茂密，给人一种未完成房地产开发的荒凉感。作者同行的地理学家对尤加利树持复杂态度，部分当地人欣赏这些树带来的常绿和秩序感，但也有不少人批评它们是“绿色沙漠”，外表美丽却缺乏生物多样性，甚至可能加剧火灾风险。

尤加利树的种植公司则强调其可持续林业认证和防火措施，认为这些树满足了全球对纸浆产品的巨大需求。然而，科技公司如苹果、微软等正探索尤加利树是否能成为可扩展的气候解决方案，通过快速生长吸收二氧化碳，以抵消其碳排放。不过，尤加利树在巴西的历史和影响仍然充满争议。

43789693.article_content:
We were losing the light, and still about 20 kilometers from the main road, when
the car shuddered and died at the edge of a strange forest.
The grove grew as if indifferent to certain unspoken rules of botany. There was no understory, no foreground or background, only the trees themselves, which grew as a wall of bare trunks that rose 100 feet or so before concluding with a burst of thick foliage near the top. The rows of trees ran perhaps the length of a New York City block and fell away abruptly on either side into untidy fields of dirt and grass. The vista recalled the husk of a failed condo development, its first apartments marooned when the builders ran out of cash.
Standing there against the setting sun, the trees were, in their odd way, also rather stunning. I had no service out here—we had just left a remote nature preserve in southwestern Brazil—but I reached for my phone anyway, for a picture. The concern on the face of my travel partner, Clariana Vilela Borzone, a geographer and translator who grew up nearby, flicked to amusement. My camera roll was already full of eucalyptus.
The trees sprouted from every hillside, along every road, and more always seemed to be coming. Across the dirt path where we were stopped, another pasture had been cleared for planting. The sparse bushes and trees that had once shaded cattle in the fields had been toppled and piled up, as if in a Pleistocene gravesite.
Borzone’s friends and neighbors were divided on the aesthetics of these groves. Some liked the order and eternal verdancy they brought to their slice of the Cerrado, a large botanical region that arcs diagonally across Brazil’s midsection. Its native savanna landscape was largely gnarled, low-slung, and, for much of the year, rather brown. And since most of that flora had been cleared decades ago for cattle pasture, it was browner and flatter still. Now that land was becoming trees. It was becoming beautiful.
Some locals say they like the order and eternal verdancy of the eucalyptus, which often stand in stark contrast to the Cerrado’s native savanna landscape.
PABLO ALBARENGA
Others considered this beauty a mirage. “Green deserts,” they called the groves, suggesting bounty from afar but holding only dirt and silence within. These were not actually forests teeming with animals and undergrowth, they charged, but at best tinder for a future megafire in a land parched, in part, by their vigorous growth. This was in fact a common complaint across Latin America: in Chile, the planted rows of eucalyptus were called the “green soldiers.” It was easy to imagine getting lost in the timber, a funhouse mirror of trunks as far as the eye could see.
The timber companies that planted these trees push back on these criticisms as caricatures of a genus that’s demonized all over the world. They point to their sustainable forestry certifications and their handsome spending on fire suppression, and to the microphones they’ve placed that record cacophonies of birds and prove the groves are anything but barren. data.author: yaiml
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讨论了近期大型语言模型（LLM）在推理能力上的进展，特别是通过强化学习（RL）方法进行的训练改进。尽管GPT-4.5和Llama 4等新模型发布，但市场反应平淡，原因在于这些模型缺乏明确的推理能力训练。相比之下，xAI和Anthropic等竞争对手通过增加推理功能（如“思考”按钮）提升了模型表现。

文章强调，单纯扩大模型规模和数据量已接近极限，而通过战略性计算投资（如强化学习）仍有提升空间。OpenAI的o3模型就是一个例子，它使用了比o1多10倍的计算资源进行训练。

文章还介绍了推理模型的基础概念、RLHF（基于人类反馈的强化学习）的基本原理、PPO（近端策略优化）等算法，以及DeepSeek-R1等模型的训练方法。作者建议，如果读者已熟悉RL和PPO等概念，可以直接阅读关于近期研究论文的总结部分，以获取更多关于训练推理模型的见解。

总体而言，文章指出推理能力的强化学习训练将成为未来LLM发展的标准实践。

A lot has happened this month, especially with the releases of new flagship models like GPT-4.5 and Llama 4. But you might have noticed that reactions to these releases were relatively muted. Why? One reason could be that GPT-4.5 and Llama 4 remain conventional models, which means they were trained without explicit reinforcement learning for reasoning.
Meanwhile, competitors such as xAI and Anthropic have added more reasoning capabilities and features into their models. For instance, both the xAI Grok and Anthropic Claude interfaces now include a âthinkingâ (or âextended thinkingâ) button for certain models that explicitly toggles reasoning capabilities.
In any case, the muted response to GPT-4.5 and Llama 4 (non-reasoning) models suggests we are approaching the limits of what scaling model size and data alone can achieve.
However, OpenAIâs recent release of the o3 reasoning model demonstrates there is still considerable room for improvement when investing compute strategically, specifically via reinforcement learning methods tailored for reasoning tasks. (According to OpenAI staff during the recent livestream, o3 used 10Ã more training compute compared to o1.)
Source: OpenAI livestream (https://openai.com/live/) on April 16, 2025
While reasoning alone isnât a silver bullet, it reliably improves model accuracy and problem-solving capabilities on challenging tasks (so far). And I expect reasoning-focused post-training to become standard practice in future LLM pipelines.
So, in this article, letâs explore the latest developments in reasoning via reinforcement learning.
This article focuses on reinforcement learning training methods used to develop and improve reasoning models
Because it is a relatively long article, I am providing a Table of Contents overview below. To navigate the table of contents, please use the slider on the left-hand side in the web view.
Understanding reasoning models
RLHF basics: where it all started
A brief introduction to PPO: RLâs workhorse algorithm
RL algorithms: from PPO to GRPO
RL reward modeling: from RLHF to RLVR
How the DeepSeek-R1 reasoning models were trained
Lessons from recent RL papers on training reasoning models
Noteworthy research papers on training reasoning models
Tip:
If you are already familiar with reasoning basics, RL, PPO, and GRPO, please feel free to directly jump ahead to the âLessons from recent RL papers on training reasoning modelsâ section, which contains summaries of interesting insights from recent reasoning research papers.
Understanding reasoning models
The big elephant in the room is, of course, the definition of reasoning. In short, reasoning is about inference and training techniques that make LLMs better at handling complex tasks.
To provide a bit more detail on how this is achieved (so far), Iâd like to define reasoning as follows:
Reasoning, in the context of LLMs, refers to the modelâs ability to produce intermediate steps before providing a final answer. This is a process that is often described as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. In CoT reasoning, the LLM explicitly generates a structured sequence of statements or computations that illustrate how it arrives at its conclusion.
And below is a figure along with the definition.
A simplified illustration of how an LLM might tackle a multi-step reasoning task. Rather than just recalling a fact, the model needs to combine several intermediate reasoning steps to arrive at the correct conclusion. The intermediate reasoning steps may or may not be shown to the user, depending on the implementation.
If you are new to reasoning models and would like a more comprehensive introduction, I recommend my previous articles:
First Look at Reasoning From Scratch: Chapter 1
Understanding Reasoning LLMs
Now, as hinted at the beginning of this section, the reasoning abilities of LLMs can be improved in two ways, as nicely illustrated in a figure from an OpenAI blog post:
Accuracy improvements can be achieved through increased training or test-time compute, where test-time compute is synonymous with inference-time compute and inference-time scaling. Source: Annotated figure from https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/
In my previous article
The State of LLM Reasoning Model Inference
, I solely focused on the test-time compute methods.
In this article, I finally want to take a closer look at the training methods.
RLHF basics: where it all started
The reinforcement learning (RL) training methods used to build and improve reasoning models are more or less related to the reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) methodology that is used to develop and align conventional LLMs. So, I want to start with a small recap of how RLHF works before discussing reasoning-specific modification based on RL-based training.
Conventional LLMs typically undergo a 3-step training procedure:
Pre-training
Supervised fine-tuning
Alignment (typically via RLHF)

TL;DR
:
c/ua
(pronounced "koo-ah", short for Computer-Use Agent) is a framework that enables AI agents to control full operating systems within high-performance, lightweight virtual containers. It delivers up to 97% native speed on Apple Silicon and works with any vision language models.
What is c/ua?
c/ua
offers two primary capabilities in a single integrated framework:
High-Performance Virtualization
- Create and run macOS/Linux virtual machines on Apple Silicon with near-native performance (up to 97% of native speed) using the
Lume CLI
with
Apple's Virtualization.Framework
.
Computer-Use Interface & Agent
- A framework that allows AI systems to observe and control these virtual environments - interacting with applications, browsing the web, writing code, and performing complex workflows.
Why Use c/ua?
Security & Isolation
: Run AI agents in fully isolated virtual environments instead of giving them access to your main system
Performance
:
Near-native performance
on Apple Silicon
Flexibility
: Run macOS or Linux environments with the same framework
Reproducibility
: Create consistent, deterministic environments for AI agent workflows
LLM Integration
: Built-in support for connecting to various LLM providers
System Requirements
Mac with Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4 series)
macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer
Python 3.10+ (required for the Computer, Agent, and MCP libraries). We recommend using Conda (or Anaconda) to create an ad hoc Python environment.
Disk space for VM images (30GB+ recommended)

If you only need the virtualization capabilities:
sudo /bin/bash -c
"
$(
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/lume/scripts/install.sh
)
"
For Lume usage instructions, refer to the
Lume documentation
.
Option 2: Full Computer-Use Agent Capabilities
If you want to use AI agents with virtualized environments:
Install the Lume CLI:
sudo /bin/bash -c
"
$(
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trycua/cua/main/libs/lume/scripts/install.sh
)
"
Pull the latest macOS CUA image:
lume pull macos-sequoia-cua:latest
Start Lume daemon service:
lume serve
Install the Python libraries:
pip install cua-computer cua-agent[all]

data.title: Some __nonstring__ Turbulence
data.author: jwilk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Linux内核开发中因新编译器版本引入新警告而引发的问题。GCC 15引入的`-Wunterminated-string-initialization`警告旨在提醒开发者未终止的字符串初始化问题，但某些情况下，开发者故意不使用终止符（NUL），如在查找表中。新警告导致了编译问题，尤其是在Fedora 42提前搭载GCC 15预发布版后，Linus Torvalds升级系统并发现内核编译出错。由于部分修复补丁未及时合并，Torvalds在发布6.15-rc3前做了紧急修改，却导致在旧版GCC上编译失败。最终，他撤回了这些更改并禁用了新警告。开发者Kees Cook对问题的处理方式提出异议，指出他已提供了解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Linux内核开发中使用测试版编译器及C语言中NUL终止字符串的讨论，涉及技术选择、开发者行为和代码安全等问题。

不同观点：
• [AceJohnny2] 和 [jaapz] 认为Linus Torvalds在此次事件中不应责备内核维护者，反而应该承认自己的错误。AceJohnny2特别指出Torvalds在未仔细审查的情况下进行了更改，并批评Fedora在新版本中使用测试版编译器。jaapz则认为Torvalds通常对维护者的批评是有理由的，但这次他应该承认错误。

• [Ukv] 质疑C语言中NUL终止字符串的设计选择，认为这种设计导致了许多问题，如字符串操作效率低、无法处理包含NUL的数据、以及潜在的安全问题。Ukv认为NUL终止字符串可能是一个不幸的设计选择，而非特性。

• [Philpax] 批评Linus Torvalds的行为，并质疑在C语言开发中为何使用字符串而不是字节数组或字面量。Philpax认为这可能是更合适的选择。

• [Incipient] 对为何在RC阶段没有发现使用测试版编译器的问题感到困惑，并提出RC版本应该通过所有官方编译器和架构的测试才能发布。

• [jey] 讨论了C语言变量初始化的问题，认为在char数组中忽略NUL终止符是错误的。bjourne对此表示赞同，并强调了C语言初学者应遵循的变量赋值规则。

• [mastax] 惊讶于Linux内核没有官方的持续集成（CI）系统，暗示这可能有助于避免类似问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于C语言中NUL终止字符串的争议是讨论的一个重点，涉及其效率和安全性问题。
• 对Linus Torvalds在事件中的行为存在批评，部分评论者认为他应为错误决定承担责任。
• 评论还涉及开发流程中的技术选择和测试实践，如使用测试版工具的合理性和RC版本的测试标准。

争议焦点：
• Linus Torvalds是否应为此次事件中的错误承担责任并承认错误。
• C语言中NUL终止字符串的设计是否合理，以及是否有更好的替代方案。

By
Jonathan Corbet
April 24, 2025
New compiler releases often bring with them new warnings; those warnings
are usually welcome, since they help developers find problems before they
turn into nasty bugs.  Adapting to new warnings can also create disruption
in the development process, though, especially when an important developer
upgrades to a new compiler at an unfortunate time.  This is just the
scenario that played out with the
6.15-rc3
kernel release
and the implementation of
-Wunterminated-string-initialization
in GCC 15.
Consider a C declaration like:
char foo[8] = "bar";
The array will be initialized with the given string, including the normal
trailing NUL byte indicating the end of the string.  Now consider this
variant:
char foo[8] = "NUL-free";
This is a legal declaration, even though the declared array now lacks the
room for the NUL byte.  That byte will simply be omitted, creating an
unterminated string.  That is often not what the developer who wrote that
code wants, and it can lead to unpleasant bugs that are not discovered
until some later time.  The
-Wunterminated-string-initialization
option emits a warning for this kind of initialization, with the result
that, hopefully, the problem — if there is a problem — is fixed quickly.
The kernel community has worked to make use of this warning and, hopefully,
eliminate a source of bugs.  There is only one little problem with the new
warning, though: sometimes the no-NUL initialization is exactly what is
wanted and intended.  See, for example,
this
declaration
from
fs/cachefiles/key.c
:
static const char cachefiles_charmap[64] =
"0123456789"			/* 0 - 9 */
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"	/* 10 - 35 */
"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"	/* 36 - 61 */
"_-"				/* 62 - 63 */
;
This
char
array is used as a lookup table, not as a string, so
there is no need for a trailing NUL byte.  GCC 15, being unaware of
that usage, will emit a false-positive warning for this declaration.  There
are many places in the kernel with declarations like this; the ACPI code,
for example, uses a lot of four-byte string arrays to handle the equally
large set of four-letter ACPI acronyms.
Naturally, there is a way to suppress the warning when it does not apply
by adding an attribute to the declaration indicating that the
char
array is not actually holding a string:
__attribute__((__nonstring__))
Within the kernel, the macro
__nonstring
is used to shorten that
attribute syntax.  Work has been ongoing, primarily by Kees Cook, to fix
all of the warnings added by GCC 15.  Many patches have been
circulated; quite a few of them are in linux-next.  Cook has also been
working with the GCC developers to improve how this annotation works and to
fix a
problem
that the kernel project ran into.  There was some time left
to get this job done, though, since GCC 15 has not actually been
released — or so Cook thought.
Fedora 42
has
been released, though, and the Fedora developers, for
better or worse, decided to include a pre-release version of GCC 15
with it as the default compiler.  The Fedora project, it seems, has decided
to follow
a venerable Red Hat tradition
with this release.  Linus Torvalds, for better or worse,
decided to update his development systems to Fedora 42 the day before
tagging and releasing 6.15-rc3.  Once he tried building the kernel with the
new compiler, though, things started to go wrong, since the relevant
patches were not yet in his repository.  Torvalds responded with a series
of changes of his own, applied directly to the mainline about two hours
before the release, to fix the problems that he had encountered.  They
included
this patch
fixing warnings in the ACPI subsystem, and
this one
fixing
several others, including the example shown above.  He then tagged and
pushed out 6.15-rc3 with those changes.
Unfortunately, his last-minute changes broke the build on any version of
GCC prior to the GCC 15 pre-release — a problem that was likely to
create a certain amount of inconvenience for any developers who were not
running Fedora 42.  So, shortly after the 6.15-rc3 release, Torvalds
tacked on
one more
patch
backing out the breaking change and disabling the new warning
altogether.
This drew
a somewhat
grumpy note
from Cook, who said that he had already sent patches fixing
all of the problems, including the build-breaking one that Torvalds ran
into.  He asked Torvalds to revert the changes and use the planned fixes,
adding: "

data.title: What If We Could Rebuild Kafka from Scratch?
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary:
Gunnar Morling探讨了如果在云环境中从头重建Kafka，哪些特性和改进是理想的。他提出以下几点：

1. **去除分区**：在云对象存储中，分区不再是必需的，建议关注消息键的全局或特定顺序，以提高灵活性和效率。
   
2. **以键为中心的访问**：实现基于消息键的高效访问和重放，支持动态调整消费者数量，并解决头部阻塞问题。

3. **主题层次结构**：借鉴Solace系统，通过结构化的主题标识符支持更高效的订阅和消息过滤。

4. **并发控制**：增加乐观锁等机制，防止基于过时数据产生的并发冲突。

5. **代理端 schema 支持**：将消息schema作为核心概念，提升用户体验并支持更广泛的数据存储格式。

6. **可扩展性和插件化**：借鉴Postgres和Kubernetes，通过定义良好的扩展点和插件合同实现系统的自定义和功能增强。

这些改进旨在使Kafka更适应云环境，提高其灵活性、效率和可维护性。

• 对Kafka的分区和并发性控制问题的讨论反映了技术实现中的实际挑战。

Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
What If We Could Rebuild Kafka From Scratch?
Posted at Apr 24, 2025
The last few days I spent some time digging into the recently announced
KIP-1150
("Diskless Kafka"), as well
AutoMQ’s Kafka fork
, tightly integrating Apache Kafka and object storage, such as S3. Following the example set by WarpStream, these projects aim to substantially improve the experience of using Kafka in cloud environments, providing better elasticity, drastically reducing cost, and paving the way towards native lakehouse integration.
This got me thinking, if we were to start all over and develop a durable cloud-native event log from scratch—​Kafka.next if you will—​which traits and characteristics would be desirable for this to have? Separating storage and compute and object store support would be table stakes, but what else should be there? Having used Kafka for many years for building event-driven applications as well as for running realtime ETL and change data capture pipelines, here’s my personal wishlist:
Do away with partitions:
topic partitions were crucial for scaling purposes when data was stored on node-local disks, but they are not required when storing data on effectively infinitely large object storage in the cloud. While partitions also provide ordering guarantees, this never struck me as overly useful from a client perspective. You either want to have global ordering of all messages on a given topic, or (more commonly) ordering of all messages with the same key. In contrast, defined ordering of otherwise unrelated messages whose key happens to yield the same partition after hashing isn’t that valuable, so there’s not much point in exposing partitions as a concept to users.
Key-centric access:
instead of partition-based access, efficient access and replay of all the messages with one and the same key would be desirable. Rather than coarse-grained scanning of all the records on a given topic or partition, let’s have millions of entity-level streams! Not only would this provide access exactly to the subset of data you need, it would also let you increase and decrease the number of consumers dynamically based on demand, not hitting the limits of a pre-defined partition count. Key-level streams (with guaranteed ordering) would be a perfect foundation for
Event Sourcing
architectures as well as actor-based and agentic systems. In addition, this approach largely solves the problem of head-of-line blocking found in partition based systems with cumulative acknowledgements: if a consumer can’t process a particular message, this will only block other messages with the same key (which oftentimes is exactly what you’d want), while all other messages are not affected. Rather than coarse-grained partitions, individual messages keys are becoming the failure domain.
Topic hierarchies:
available in systems like
Solace
, topic hierarchies promote parts of the message payload into structured path-like topic identifiers, allowing for clients to subscribe to arbitrary sub sets of all the available streams based on patterns in an efficient way, without requiring brokers to deserialize and parse entire messages.
Means of concurrency control:
As is, using Kafka as a system of record can be problematic as you can’t prevent writing messages which are based on an outdated view of the stored data. Concurrency control, for instance via optimistic locking of message keys, would help to detect and fence off concurrent conflicting writes. That way, when a message gets acknowledged successfully, it is guaranteed that it has been produced seeing the latest state of that key, avoiding lost updates.
Broker-side schema support:
Kafka treats messages as opaque byte arrays with arbitrary content, requiring out-of-bands propagation of message schemas to consumers. This can be especially problematic when erroneous (or malicious) producers send non-conformant data. Also, without additional tooling, the current architecture prevents Kafka data from being written to open table formats such as Apache Iceberg. For all these reasons, Kafka is used with a schema registry most of the time, but making schema support a first-class concept would allow for better user ergonomics—​for instance, Kafka could expose
AsyncAPI-compatible metadata
out of the box—​and also open the door for storing data in different ways, for instance in a columnar representation.
Extensibility and pluggability:
a common trait of many successful open-source projects like Postgres or Kubernetes is their extensibility. Users and integrators can customize the behavior of the system by providing implementations of well-defined extension points and plug-in contracts, rather than by modifying the system’s core itself (following the

2. **以键为中心的访问**：实现基于消息键的高效访问和重放，支持动态调整消费者数量，并解决头部阻塞问题。

3. **主题层次结构**：借鉴Solace系统，通过结构化的主题标识符支持更高效的订阅和消息过滤。

4. **并发控制**：增加乐观锁等机制，防止基于过时数据产生的并发冲突。

5. **代理端 schema 支持**：将消息schema作为核心概念，提升用户体验并支持更广泛的数据存储格式。

6. **可扩展性和插件化**：借鉴Postgres和Kubernetes，通过定义良好的扩展点和插件合同实现系统的自定义和功能增强。

这些改进旨在使Kafka更适应云环境，提高其灵活性、效率和可维护性。

data.title: Finland is painting deer antlers with reflective paint (2014)
data.author: andrewfromx
data.article_summary: 每年约有4,000只驯鹿在芬兰的道路上因车祸丧生，造成1,500万欧元的损失。为减少事故，芬兰驯鹿牧民协会正试验在驯鹿的鹿角上喷涂反光漆，以提高它们在司机眼中的可见性。目前该喷涂正在毛发上测试，但可能在鹿角上更有效，因为鹿角可以从各个角度被看到。大多数事故发生在11月、12月以及7月、8月。与其他尝试通过改善道路和车辆安全来防止碰撞不同，芬兰直接在动物身上进行试验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何减少野生动物（特别是鹿）与车辆碰撞的讨论

不同观点：
• **关于鹿的种类的混淆**：
   - [fifilura] 认为文章标题应使用“驯鹿”而非“鹿”，因为驯鹿是由萨米人驯养的，更容易被控制和标记。
   - [jmclnx] 和 [vanattab] 指出驯鹿和某些鹿种（如白尾鹿）每年都会脱落鹿角，这意味着每年都需要重新标记或绘画，这在实际操作中可能不可行。

• **关于具体方法的可行性**：
   - [spcldvlpr] 和 [bethekidyouwant] 提到给驯鹿角涂漆的实验失败了，因为油漆无法持久，且每年重新涂漆在操作上非常困难。
   - [vanattab] 进一步解释鹿角的生长周期，指出只有在特定时间段才能进行标记，有效时间很短。

• **其他国家的尝试和科技手段**：
   - [pelagic_sky] 提到澳大利亚使用虚拟围栏来减少野生动物与车辆碰撞的尝试，通过声音和灯光警示动物。
   - [blutack] 分享了英国新森林国家公园为自由漫步的小马佩戴反光项圈的成功案例。
   - [aiauthoritydev] 建议使用野生动物摄像机和道路信号来警示驾驶员。

• **基因工程的讨论**：
   - [ajb] 提出通过基因工程使鹿具备荧光特性，以解决标记问题，但也提到释放转基因动物的伦理和安全问题。

补充讨论：
• **对文章质量的批评**：
   - [DontchaKnowit] 对文章的内容和信息量不满，认为缺乏实质性信息。
   - [DuckOnFire] 以幽默的方式想象驯鹿看到同伴发光的鹿角的情景，增添了讨论的趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 给驯鹿角涂漆或标记是否具有实际可操作性和持续性是主要争议点，特别是在考虑鹿角每年脱落的情况下。此外，使用科技手段如基因工程或反光材料的具体效果和可行性也在讨论中存在分歧。

43747634.article_content:
Can you see me now?
Anne Ollila
Every year, about 4,000 reindeer lose their lives on Finnish roads in car accidents, causing 15 million Euros of damage every year. And now, the Finnish Reindeer Herders Association is testing out a new way to make the large mammals more visible to drivers: reflective paint.
The idea is to spray the antlers of reindeer with reflective paint that reflects motorists’ headlights.
"The aim is to prevent traffic accidents. The spray is being tested on fur at the moment, but it may be even more effective on the antlers, because they are seen from every side," Anne Ollila, chairwoman of the
Reindeer Herders Association
,
told the Finnish news source YLE
.
According to the Finnish paper Helsinging Sanomat
, most collisions occur in November and December when the roads are icy and it gets dark earlier. July and August are also bad months, as the mosquitos “keep the deer on the move.”
Most of the time, attempts to keep motorists from hitting animals center around making cars and roads safer.
One proposal in Canada
suggested painting the a series of reflective pinstripes across all the the lanes, that would help motorists see crossing moose. But the Finns are heading straight to the source, and painting the animals themselves.

data.author: cryptoz
data.article_summary: 近期，剑桥大学的Nikku Madhusudhan及其同事分析詹姆斯·韦伯空间望远镜的数据后声称，距地球124光年的超级地球K2-18b的大气中发现了二甲基硫化物，这种气体在地球上仅由生物产生，暗示可能存在外星生命。然而，新的分析表明，这些迹象可能仅仅是统计噪声，而非确凿证据。天文学家仍在探索这一神秘信号的真正原因。与此同时，其他科学发现也在不断推进对宇宙和生命起源的理解。

主要讨论点：关于网页存档服务（如Archive.today）的可靠性、用途及隐私问题的讨论。

不同观点：

• **支持存档服务的观点**：
   - **信息保存**：jnord支持使用存档服务，认为它能够有效保存网页内容，防止因网站关闭或内容被修改而丢失重要信息。例如，存档可以保存新闻文章，以备日后查阅。
   - **研究与验证**：存档服务对于学术研究和事实核查非常有用。通过存档，研究者可以访问原始信息，验证引用的准确性，避免因网页更新或删除而导致的信息失真。

• **反对存档服务的观点**：
   - **隐私问题**：反对者担心存档服务可能会无意中保存包含个人隐私或敏感信息的网页，导致这些信息被公开传播，侵犯个人隐私权。
   - **版权问题**：有人指出，存档服务可能涉及侵犯版权，因为它在未经原创作者或版权持有者许可的情况下复制和分发内容。

• **中立及条件支持的观点**：

• **争议焦点**：存档服务在保护信息和侵犯隐私、版权之间的界限是主要争议点。如何在信息自由和个人权利之间取得平衡是讨论的核心。

• **实际案例**：讨论中有人提到了一些具体案例，例如某些有争议的网页被存档后引发的法律纠纷，或因存档服务错误导致的信息误传。

data.title: New Linux Rootkit
data.author: watermelon0
data.article_summary: 一家公司发布了一种名为“Curing”的Linux rootkit，它利用Linux内核中的io_uring功能，绕过许多现有的监控系统调用检测方案，进行隐秘的恶意活动，如建立网络连接或篡改文件。这揭示了当前依赖系统调用监控的网络安全方案的漏洞。发布该研究的ARMO公司声称其产品可以防御此类攻击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在特定情况下是否应采取更严格的措施以避免潜在风险的讨论

不同观点：
• 一位用户认为，在某些情况下采取更严格的措施是必要的，以防止小概率但高风险的事件发生。他以“瑞士奶酪模型”为例，强调多层保护的重要性，特别是在安全领域。
• 另一位用户则认为，过度严格的措施可能会导致不必要的负担和成本，特别是在资源有限的情况下。他质疑是否所有潜在风险都值得进行提前预防。
• 一位支持严格措施的用户指出，某些行业，如航空业，采用严格的措施是因为它们有效减少了事故的发生。他认为这种做法可以应用于其他高风险领域。
• 反对严格措施的用户反驳说，航空业的例子不具备普遍性，因为航空业有较高的安全需求和充足的资源，而其他行业可能不具备同样的条件。

43790405.article_content:
New Linux Rootkit
Interesting
:
The company has released a working rootkit called “Curing” that uses io_uring, a feature built into the Linux kernel, to stealthily perform malicious activities without being caught by many of the detection solutions currently on the market.
At the heart of the issue is the heavy reliance on monitoring system calls, which has become the go-to method for many cybersecurity vendors. The problem? Attackers can completely sidestep these monitored calls by leaning on io_uring instead. This clever method could let bad actors quietly make network connections or tamper with files without triggering the usual alarms.
Here’s
the code.
Note the self-serving nature of this announcement: ARMO, the company that released the research and code, has a product that it claims blocks this kind of attack.

data.title: Shortest-possible walking tour to 81,998 bars in South Korea
data.author: geeknews
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了通过解决旅行商问题（TSP），找到韩国81,998个酒吧的最短步行路线。使用开源路由机器（OSRM）计算出3,361,795,003个点对点 travel times，最终得出总步行时间为15,386,117秒，约178天。该路线是经过验证的最优解，打破了此前荷兰57,912个站点的记录。计算结合了LKH代码和Concorde代码，以确保解的质量和效率。文章还讨论了TSP问题的复杂性及P vs NP问题，强调了这种大规模TSP实例的可解性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对大规模旅行商问题（TSP）解决方案的讨论，特别是涉及近82,000个酒吧的TSP实例。

不同观点：
• [gku] 强调了同一作者提供的涉及13.3亿颗星的TSP解决方案，指出其路线长度是最短可能路线的1.0038倍，展示了该解决方案的高效性。
• [Animats] 提出了使用贝尔实验室的简单概率算法与经典TSP方法的比较，认为尽管后者不保证最优解，但对于大多数实际问题已经足够接近最优。
• [noduerme] 对未提及总距离表示困惑，认为知道实际距离有助于理解路径的偏离程度，并提出对卡路里消耗的计算感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [notesinthefield] 对近82,000个酒吧的数量感到惊讶，并将这个问题与一个面积相当于俄亥俄州的国家相比较。
• [tiernano] 分享了一个有趣的相关问题，提到如何在不经过酒吧的情况下从一地到另一地，增加了讨论的趣味性。
• [pugworthy] 描述了自己在COVID期间使用CityStrides追踪器步行探索城镇街道的个人经验，认为手动规划路线是乐趣的一部分，并提到一些人完成了惊人的步行量。
• [OsrsNeedsf2P] 对找到如此困难的数据集表示印象深刻，但也提到在计算资源和完成度之间的平衡问题。
• [rurban] 回顾了TSP问题在历史上的进展，从最大13到目前的31,780个点，并建议使用CUDA而非普通C语言来实现。
• [blt] 赞赏了分支定界算法，认为它简单而有用。
• [flerchin] 以幽默的方式指出酒吧的变动可能需要重新计算TSP路径。
• [DennisL123] 作为OSRM的主要开发者，对大规模TSP实例的解决表示赞赏。
• [mofunnyman] 计算出如果一生访问所有酒吧，每天需要访问5.616个酒吧，认为这非常疯狂。
• [Catagris] 提到在其附近有些地点未被标记在地图上，指出了数据完整性的潜在问题。
• [BrtByte] 认为涉及近82,000个酒吧的TSP解决方案既有趣又令人印象深刻，兼具数学和啤酒的魅力。
• [HPsquared] 提出了寻找最长可能路径的相反问题，引发了新的思考方向。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中没有明显的争议，但有对算法效率、计算资源使用以及数据完整性的不同看法和兴趣点。

43778105.article_content:
korea81998
Shortest-possible walking tour to 81,998 bars in South Korea
Visiting the many bars in Seoul.
Click.
Line drawing of the tour.
Click.
Daejeon, home of IBS and KAIST.
Click.
Locations of bars in Korea.
Click.
UK Pubs TSP in Korean magazine
Math Dong-A
.
Click.
Previous
Next
We have solved a traveling salesman problem (TSP) to walk to 81,998 bars in South Korea.
The problem was created using the
Open Source Routing Machine
(OSRM) to build a table of the 3,361,795,003 point-to-point travel times, one for each pair of bar locations.
Our computation produced a tour together with a proof that it is a shortest-possible route to visit all 81,998 stops when measured with the OSRM times.
It would be a very long pub crawl.
The total walking time for the round trip is 15,386,177 seconds, or 178 days, 1 hour, 56 minutes, and 17 seconds.
You will need to stop for plenty of drinks along the way (better stick with water, tea, or Diet Coke if you want to finish the route in only a few years), so it's  not likely you would count every second on such a journey.
But the level of precision makes the point that this not just a good route, it is an optimal solution to the 81,998-stop TSP.
It is not possible to rearrange the order of stops to save even a single second of the OSRM-estimated walking time.
This is the largest road-map instance of the TSP that has been solved to provable optimality, exceeding the
57,912-stop tour through the Netherlands
solved in February 2021.
The computations were carried out between December 2024 and March 2025 at
Roskilde University
and at the
University of Waterloo
.
Details of the computing work can be found on the
Computation
page.
Interactive map
The figure below is a screen shot of an interactive map of the korea81998 tour.
The menu on the left-hand-side lets you select one of seven regions to view.
At the top right-hand-side you can choose to have either a colored street map or a grayscale map without street labels.
Just below this menu you can select whether or not to display the stop markers, or to display the tour edges, or to display both.
You can view the map by clicking on the image.
Snapshots of the Tour
If you have trouble viewing the interactive map, you can click on the drawings below to see high-resolution images of the tour.
For close-up views of city regions, please see the
Cities
page.
Optimality
Newspapers, popular journals, blogs, and scientific press releases regularly report that solving even tiny instances of the TSP is impossible with the current generation of computers.
A typical example is the following quote from the Washington Post.
"It would take a laptop computer 1,000 years to compute the most efficient route between 22 cities, for example."
Quantum computers may be more of an imminent threat than AI,
Washington Post
, February 5, 2018.
Statements such as this assume the only way to solve the TSP is to check each possible tour, one-by-one.
That clearly cannot work for any of the large instances of the TSP we have solved.
The number of tours in the korea81998 case is roughly
2 followed by 367308 zeroes
.
This huge number of possible solutions is frightening, but it doesn't mean we can't solve this large example of the TSP.
Our approach combines the
LKH
code for computing extremely good TSP solutions and the
Concorde
code for applying what is known as the "cutting-plane method" for producing quality guarantees.
You can see a short discussion of how we apply these tools on the
Computation
page.
For a quick glimpse of the cutting-plane method, here is how I describe the process in a
short piece in Scientific American
"The idea is to follow Yogi Berra's advice `When you come to a fork in the road, take it.' A tool called linear programming allows us to do just this, assigning fractions to roads joining pairs of cities, rather than deciding immediately whether to use a road or not. It is perfectly fine, in this model, to send half a salesman along both branches of the fork."
"The process begins with the requirement that, for every city, the fractions assigned to the arriving and departing roads each sum to one. Then, step-by-step, further restrictions are added, each involving sums of fractions assigned to roads. Linear programming eventually points us to the best decision for each road, and thus the shortest possible route."
If you have a few minutes, you can check out the video of the talk
Optimal Tours
given at the
National Museum of Mathematics
, where the method is described in detail.
Or, keeping with the Korean theme, please have a look at video of the talk
Amazon Deliveries, Pub Walks, and Astro Tours
, given at
KAIST
in March 2024.
P vs NP
A great discussion of the P and NP complexity classes, including connections to the TSP, can be found in Lance Fortnow's article
Fifty Years of P vs. NP and the Possibility of the Impossible
.
Credit: https://cacm.acm.org/research/fifty-years-of-p-vs-np-and-the-possibility-of-the-impossible/

data.title: Avoiding Skill Atrophy in the Age of AI
data.author: NotInOurNames
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）对学习和编程的影响，包括其潜在的好处和风险

不同观点：
• gchamonlive认为LLM并没有改变学习的本质，只是放大了人们的意图。对于有意学习的人，LLM是一个强大的工具，但若仅用于伪装知识，可能会加速知识的衰退。
• rjknight指出，使用LLM需要更清晰地解释意图和完全理解问题，这迫使他们在编码前进行更多思考。然而，LLM快速生成代码的能力可能导致问题被忽视，直到生成大量代码后才被发现。
• gherkinnn表示，LLM可以帮助揭示思维中的漏洞，但理解问题本质依然不可或缺。LLM可以作为一个可靠的橡皮鸭或侦探，但不能替代深度理解。
• AdventureMouse认为，LLM的主要价值在于帮助梳理自己的思维过程，而不是提供黑箱答案。将LLM视为神谕并试图外包理解问题会导致挫败感。
• bluetomcat警告，LLM可能导致人类知识的同质化，简单问题被通用解决方案取代，可能脱离具体环境。
• TedHerman提到，技术工具的进步可能导致某些心智技能的丧失，比如手写、艺术和音乐，但想象力的丧失将是最难恢复的。
• bgwalter预测，平均智商可能会在未来十年下降，但人们的生产力可能会因AI生成内容而看似提高。
• Saigonautica认为，保持自然好奇心和手动构建事物的过程是避免技能衰退的关键。AI可以是有趣的工具，但不应取代核心过程。
• dmazin指出，有关技能衰退的文章与自己之前的博客内容相似，并希望原文能更明确地引用。
• sunshine-o强调，亲手完成任务带来的成就感和幸福感是人类进化和生存的核心，AI/UBI社会可能加剧现有问题。
• hnthrowaway0315认为，有些文档对新手不友好，LLM可以帮助解决阅读文档的困难。
• heymax054使用Anki和LLM结合，避免技能/知识衰退。
• adidoit担心依赖自动化会导致技能衰退和失败，提出需要更多AI教练来增加挑战和摩擦，帮助防止批判性思维的衰退。
• Aeolun认为，即使个人避免技能丧失，若AI服务下线，开发进度仍可能停滞。未来高级程序员的工作将部分在于指导AI，并逐步转向100%人类指导。
• qwertox分享了在没有AI帮助的手动编码经验，发现自己依然能够高效完成任务，但速度较慢。

补充讨论：
• LLM作为工具的潜力和风险：帮助理解问题与可能导致知识外包的争议。
• 技能衰退与知识同质化的担忧：技术进步可能导致某些技能的丧失和知识的单一化。
• 个人经验与策略：不同用户使用LLM的具体方法和感受，包括结合传统学习工具和保持自然好奇心的重要性。
• 批判性思维的培养：提出增加挑战和摩擦以防止思维能力衰退的必要性。

data.title: GCC, the GNU Compiler Collection 15.1 released
data.author: jrepinc
data.article_summary: GCC 15.1已于2025年4月25日发布，是GNU编译器集合的重大更新版本，包含新功能及多项改进。GCC最初代表GNU C Compiler，但现在支持多种编程语言。此次发布感谢了众多贡献者，他们是GCC成功的重要支持者。更多信息可访问GCC项目网站或联系开发邮件列表。获取GCC可通过镜像站点或版本控制系统。使用问题可查阅GCC手册或联系帮助邮箱。反馈欢迎发送至开发者列表。本文可自由复制，但需保留版权声明。页面由GCC团队维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C/C++编程语言中的语法和编译器行为变化，以及新特性

不同观点：
• Calavar认为，C/C++中对union的{0}初始化器行为改变（不再保证整个union，包括填充位的清零）会无声地破坏大量现有代码，尤其是基于union的类型变换代码。他们指出，过去{0}能保证整个union清零，而{}不能，但现在情况反转，这令人困惑。Calavar建议，为了不破坏旧代码，应该让{0}和{}都对整个union进行零初始化。

• Omoikane则对C语言中新增的#embed指令表示兴奋，并引用了C23标准中的相关支持，以及C++中P1967R14提案（#embed）的进展。他们关注的是新特性的实现和其在标准中的位置。

• Elvircrn对C++模块的改进表示疑问，希望能了解这些“重大改进”具体是什么。这里反映出对新特性的具体内容和实际效果缺乏清晰的信息。

• Codr7关注的是musttail属性，表示期待尝试该特性。这表明对编译器优化和新功能的积极态度。

补充讨论：
• 对于union初始化行为的改变，Calavar提出了对旧代码兼容性的担忧，并提到这可能需要开发者修改代码或依赖特定编译器选项（如-fzero-init-padding-bits=unions）来恢复旧行为。

• 讨论中涉及的标准和提案链接（如#embed的Hacker News讨论）显示出社区对新标准特性的关注和讨论热度。

• 总体来看，评论反映了开发者对语言标准变化的适应过程，以及对新特性具体实现和兼容性问题的关注。

data.author: richardfontana
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一份要求开放源代码促进会（OSI）公布2025年董事会选举完整结果的请愿书。请愿者对OSI在选举后移除部分候选人选票并公布修改后的结果表示担忧，认为此举损害了OSI的公信力。具体来说，OSI在2025年选举后排除了三名候选人的选票，其中包括主张改革的Bradley Kuhn和Richard Fontana。请愿者指出，选举规则在过程中被改变，且结果被修改，这破坏了选举的公正性。他们呼吁OSI以透明方式公布完整、未经修改的选举结果，以恢复其 integrity 和声誉。请愿书强调透明度对OSI的健康发展至关重要，不涉及对特定候选人或政策立场的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放源代码和开放源代码促进会（OSI）的定位与作用，特别是在企业影响下的演变和争议。

不同观点：
• **tedivm的观点**：认为开放源代码AI定义（OSAID）是对开放源代码社区的背叛。其主要论据是允许公司重新定义“开放”，以包括封闭组件，违背了OSI应该代表的理念。批评这是为了让大公司将其封闭模型伪装成开放。

• **remon的观点**：对OSI的实际作用提出疑问。作为多个开源项目的参与者，remon表示在合规、治理、教育等方面从未见到OSI被提及，质疑其存在的影响力。

• **lolinder的观点**：回顾OSI的成立背景，指出其初衷是作为企业友好的替代方案，以替代斯塔尔曼的自由软件基金会（FSF）。lolinder认为，OSI的演变是将“自由软件”的道德框架淡化，以更迎合企业的商业利益。lolinder主张，要解决自由和开源软件（FOSS）运动中的问题，需要摆脱企业影响，回归以道德为基础的自由软件运动，并指出GPL和AGPL许可证是少数未被企业利益吞噬的许可证，因为它们基于深厚的伦理原则。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：OSI是否应该允许公司将封闭组件定义为开放，以及其在现代开源和自由软件运动中的角色和影响力。tedivm和lolinder明显反对企业对开源定义的影响，而remon则对OSI的存在和作用提出质疑。

• **历史背景**：lolinder提供了OSI成立时的背景信息，强调其从一开始就是作为企业友好选项，与自由软件基金会的道德立场形成对比。这一历史视角为当前的争议提供了背景支持。

• **许可证讨论**：lolinder特别提到GPL和AGPL许可证，认为它们是少数未被企业利益影响的许可证，强调其基于伦理原则，与开放源代码的商业化趋势形成对比。

README.md
Petition to the Open Source Initiative: Publish the Full 2025 Election Results
We, the undersigned, petition the Open Source Initiative
(OSI) to release the complete, unaltered results of its 2025 Board of
Directors elections
. We believe that by removing candidates and votes
after
voting concluded, OSI has damaged its credibility.
We call for transparency as a first step toward repairing
OSI's integrity and reputation.
Background context
OSI relies entirely on community deference and respect
for its authority in promoting Open Source and the
consistent use of the term "Open Source."
In 2012, OSI shifted toward operating as a member-driven organization.
Every year since 2013, OSI has held elections where Individual and Affiliate members
vote on directors to represent them.
Although OSI is not legally bound to accept the results,
the elections have been a key part of community and membership engagement,
and OSI has always worked to follow best practices for public elections.
Until 2025, OSI has published the full results of elections.
2025 election
In 2025, OSI excluded all votes for three candidates before publishing results.
The announcement of the
altered voting results
did not name the removed candidates, but they were Bentley Hensel,
Bradley Kuhn, and Richard Fontana (incidentally, a former OSI director).
Notably, Kuhn and Fontana campaigned on a joint
OSI Reform platform
which included four proposals, the most significant being a call to repeal
the newly-adopted Open Source AI Definition (OSAID).
They also advocated for revising the
OSI Board Member Agreement
,
because they interpreted the clause requiring members to "support publicly all Board
decisions" as being overly expansive and stifling. They proposed clarifying or
limiting the clause to achieve a better balance.
Normally, as in prior years, as with other organizations, and as stated during
candidate orientation, signing of the Board Agreement would happen only
with the election winners as part of getting seated as new directors.
Kuhn and Fontana say that they brought up their concerns about the Agreement
during candidate orientation and came away with the understanding that they
would be able to discuss how to resolve the issue later if they won the election.
Then,
about one hour after voting ended, OSI emailed a
new
requirement
to the 11 non-incumbent candidates. They gave a 47-hour deadline for all to
sign the board member agreement or be disqualified.
Hensel missed the deadline simply by not checking his email soon enough.
Having no chance to otherwise resolve or discuss their agreement
concerns, Fontana and Kuhn returned signed board member agreements that included
their proposed changes. OSI then published the announcement which
excluded all votes for the three candidates.
Ramifications
In general, changing election rules mid-process and altering vote counts
undermines the integrity of any election.
Results must be published transparently — regardless of whether a
candidate withdraws, dies, or is disqualified for any reason. Once a
candidate appears on the ballot, the only way to respect voters is to
count and report the votes as cast. Presenting altered voting results
misrepresents
and disrespects the electorate.
Regardless of particular concerns about the Board Agreement, for the
current OSI Board to remove critical candidates while hiding
the voting results presents a clear conflict of interest and invites
community speculation about motives and corruption. As
LWN
OSI election coverage
noted, "a cynical person might conclude that the last-minute
requirement to sign the agreement was to disqualify one or both because
they would have won otherwise; and that the OSI leadership was unwilling
to have even a minority number of board members who might seek to steer
the ship in a different direction."
Call for resolution
We are community members who care deeply about OSI’s mission.
We want to see OSI governed with integrity and transparency.
This petition does not endorse particular candidates or policy positions.
We believe that everyone should care about transparency

• **lolinder的观点**：回顾OSI的成立背景，指出其初衷是作为企业友好的替代方案，以替代斯塔尔曼的自由软件基金会（FSF）。lolinder认为，OSI的演变是将“自由软件”的道德框架淡化，以更迎合企业的商业利益。lolinder主张，要解决自由和开源软件（FOSS）运动中的问题，需要摆脱企业影响，回归以道德为基础的自由软件运动，并指出GPL和AGPL许可证是少数未被企业利益吞噬的许可证，因为它们基于深厚的伦理原则。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：OSI是否应该允许公司将封闭组件定义为开放，以及其在现代开源和自由软件运动中的角色和影响力。tedivm和lolinder明显反对企业对开源定义的影响，而remon则对OSI的存在和作用提出质疑。

• **历史背景**：lolinder提供了OSI成立时的背景信息，强调其从一开始就是作为企业友好选项，与自由软件基金会的道德立场形成对比。这一历史视角为当前的争议提供了背景支持。

• **许可证讨论**：lolinder特别提到GPL和AGPL许可证，认为它们是少数未被企业利益影响的许可证，强调其基于伦理原则，与开放源代码的商业化趋势形成对比。

data.title: The hidden cost of AI coding
data.author: Sharpie4679
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了使用AI编写代码的潜在隐形成本，即对编程乐趣和成就感的削弱。作者回顾了过去编程带来的“心流”体验——那种全神贯注、创造和解决问题的快乐。然而，随着AI工具的广泛应用，编程变得更高效，但也更被动，开发者逐渐从“创作者”转变为“策展人”，通过提示调整AI生成的代码。作者担心这种转变可能导致开发者失去深层次的满足感，即使工作更高效，但幸福感可能下降。文章最后提出，或许需要重新理解在AI辅助的时代，如何在更高层次的思考和创造中找到新的快乐和成就感。

不同观点：

43775358.article_content:
The Hidden Cost of AI Coding
“The best moments in our lives are not the passive, receptive, relaxing times… The best moments usually occur if a person’s body or mind is stretched to its limits in a voluntary effort to accomplish something difficult and worthwhile.”
— Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
I know I’ve posted some upbeat content about AI before,
celebrating its potential
and
encouraging teams to embrace these tools
. And honestly, I still believe in that future. But today I want to share something more personal, more nuanced — the one thing that currently worries me most about using AI for software development:
lack of joy
.
It’s easy to talk about productivity gains, competitive advantages, and how AI will reshape our industry.
We’ve had those conversations
. What’s harder to discuss is what might be lost along the way – something intangible but vital to many of us who chose this profession not just for the paycheck, but because we genuinely love the craft of programming.
It’s 8:47 AM, fresh coffee steams on the table, and my headphones cocoon me in the perfect playlist. I go to Asana, where I know
exactly
what I need to do that day. I open Neovim and code starts
flowing
through me. I’ve lost the sense of time; I’m completely present in the moment.
That, my friends, is what I used to describe as a happy work day. I’m sure that some of you will resonate.
Those days I’d emerge tired but fulfilled. Something about the direct connection between thought and creation — where my fingers were simply the conduit for translating ideas into working software — felt almost transcendent. The struggle to solve problems, the small victories along the way, and the satisfaction of building something from nothing… these weren’t just aspects of the job; they were the reason I fell in love with programming in the first place.
This experience I’m describing is what psychologists call “flow” — a mental state where you’re fully immersed in an activity, energized by deep focus and complete involvement. First described by
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
(the psychologist I quoted at the beginning), flow is that sweet spot where challenge meets skill, where the task at hand is neither too easy (causing boredom) nor too difficult (causing anxiety). It’s a state strongly associated with creativity, productivity, and most importantly — happiness. For software developers, it’s that magical zone where problems become puzzles rather than obstacles, where hours pass like minutes, and where the boundary between you and your code seems to dissolve.
Fast forward to today, and that joy of coding is decreasing rapidly. Well, I’m a manager these days, so there’s that… But even when I do get technical, I usually just open Cursor and prompt my way out of 90% of it. It’s way more productive, but more passive as well.
Instead of that deep immersion where I’d craft each function, I’m now more like a
curator
? I describe what I want, evaluate what the AI gives me, tweak the prompts, and iterate. It’s efficient, yes. Revolutionary, even. But something essential feels missing — that state of flow where time vanishes and you’re completely absorbed in creation. If this becomes the dominant workflow across teams, do we risk an industry full of highly productive yet strangely detached developers?
So that’s what I’m worried about, and honestly, I have no idea what to think of it. On one hand, it’s clear to me that people using AI tools
are
more productive. On the other hand, I worry about long-term happiness and joy in their craft when they’re simply hitting tab to generate code rather than writing it themselves.
When we outsource the parts of programming that used to demand our complete focus and creativity, do we also outsource the opportunity for satisfaction? Can we find the same fulfillment in prompt engineering that we once found in problem-solving through code?
Perhaps what we need is a new understanding of where happiness can exist in this AI-augmented world. Maybe the joy doesn’t have to disappear completely — it just shifts. Instead of finding delight in writing the perfect algorithm, perhaps we’ll discover satisfaction in the higher-level thinking about system design, in the creative process of describing exactly what we want to build, or in the human aspects of software development that AI can’t touch.
I don’t have all the answers. But maybe, just maybe, we need to be intentional about preserving (some) spaces in our work where flow can still happen — where we still code by hand sometimes, not because it’s efficient, but because it make us happy.
After all, if we lose the joy in our craft, what exactly are we optimizing for?

data.title: Privacy folks – what's your take on using LLMs at work?
data.author: adeebaslam
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在处理公共和私有数据时的隐私与安全问题，以及是否应依赖专有模型或本地模型。

不同观点：
• [whs] 认为只应使用LLM搜索公共信息，不应用其处理专有数据。同时，他对模型训练数据中包含其代码表示不满，认为这违反了版权，特别是在未遵循相关许可的情况下。
• [gbraad] 不信任将代理（agent）用于处理客户代码或个人身份信息（PII）。他选择在虚拟机或容器中运行代码，以避免本地激活相关工具。
• [bnolsen] 建议可以在本地运行LLM，但要注意版权问题。他批评依赖专有工具提升技能的做法，认为这是LLM提供商为了收回投资而采取的策略。
• [AaronAPU] 对隐私保护持怀疑态度，尤其不信任自称为“隐私AI”的公司。
• [mvieira38] 表示已经放弃完全保护隐私的努力，选择使用ChatGPT并接受其隐私设置，尽管不完全信任它们。
• [jart] 推荐使用本地运行且保护隐私的LLM，如Mozilla的llamafile。
• [HelloUsername] 没有直接回答问题，但提供了一个可能相关的链接供参考。
• [rabid_turtle] 表示只会在LLM中输入可以公开的信息，不担心LLM知道其正在进行的编码项目。
• [hengheng] 质疑云服务在隐私方面与本地服务的竞争，暗示云服务可能成为“蜜罐”（吸引攻击的目标）。
• [underseacables] 提到曾询问LLM是否会保护其数据隐私，LLM给出了肯定的回答，但对其可信度表示不确定。
• [fortyseven] 避免使用云服务，只在本地运行LLM，除非像GitHub Copilot这样由雇主支付且早期就使用的工具。
• [axegon_] 对法国公司Mistral持相对信任态度，因为其需遵守GDPR。总体上更倾向于本地运行LLM，认为数据若需联网处理，便不再完全属于自己。
• [rhabarba] 对使用LLM持否定态度，尤其在工作环境中，建议不要使用。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于是否信任LLM提供商对隐私的保护，尤其是当模型用于处理专有代码或敏感信息时。
- 一些用户（如gbraad、fortyseven）更倾向于在本地或受控环境中运行LLM，以避免隐私泄露。
- 版权问题也被提及，尤其是当用户的代码被包含在训练数据中而未遵循相关许可时。
- 对云服务和本地运行的LLM在隐私保护方面的优劣存在不同看法。

data.title: New C++ features in GCC 15
data.author: jrepinc
data.article_summary:
GCC 15.1预计于2025年4月或5月发布，包含多项C++前端的新特性，但默认仍是-std=gnu++17，可通过选项启用C++23或C++26特性。C++20、C++23和C++26特性在GCC 15中仍为实验性。

主要新特性包括：
1. **包索引**：允许直接索引模板参数包，如`pack...[N]`。
2. **结构化绑定的属性**：可在结构化绑定中添加属性，如`auto [a, b [[gnu::deprecated]]] = s;`。
3. **带理由的deleted函数**：可为被删除的函数提供一个解释消息，如`=delete("reason")`。
4. **可变参数友元**：允许使用参数包声明友元，如`friend Ts...;`。
5. **constexpr中的placement new**：C++26允许在constexpr环境中使用placement new。
6. **作为条件的结构化绑定声明**：允许在`if`/`while`/`for`/`switch`条件中使用结构化绑定声明。

这些新特性增强了C++的表达能力和编译时计算能力。GCC 16计划将默认标准切换为C++20。

• ashvardanian对`#embed`指令的引入表示欢迎，并同时提到修复范围基础`for`循环中的未定义行为（UB）也是一个不错的改进。这显示出他关注的范围更广，既关注新功能的引入，也关注代码稳定性和正确性的提升。

43792348.article_summary:
GCC 15.1预计于2025年4月或5月发布，包含多项C++前端的新特性，但默认仍是-std=gnu++17，可通过选项启用C++23或C++26特性。C++20、C++23和C++26特性在GCC 15中仍为实验性。

主要新特性包括：
1. **包索引**：允许直接索引模板参数包，如`pack...[N]`。
2. **结构化绑定的属性**：可在结构化绑定中添加属性，如`auto [a, b [[gnu::deprecated]]] = s;`。
3. **带理由的deleted函数**：可为被删除的函数提供一个解释消息，如`=delete("reason")`。
4. **可变参数友元**：允许使用参数包声明友元，如`friend Ts...;`。
5. **constexpr中的placement new**：C++26允许在constexpr环境中使用placement new。
6. **作为条件的结构化绑定声明**：允许在`if`/`while`/`for`/`switch`条件中使用结构化绑定声明。

这些新特性增强了C++的表达能力和编译时计算能力。GCC 16计划将默认标准切换为C++20。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对创业失败和个人困境，是否应该暂停或放弃当前的创业项目。

不同观点：
• **暂停创业，寻找稳定工作**：多位评论者（如alissa_v、hardwaresofton、adrianmsmith、asimpleusecase）建议暂时将创业放在次要位置，寻找一份全职或合同工作以获得财务稳定。他们认为当前的创业压力和个人困境（如失去亲人的悲痛）让继续创业变得不切实际。找到稳定收入后，可以重新审视创业项目或在未来再次尝试。

• **继续尝试创业，但调整策略**：部分评论者（如leandot、csomar、zenyc）建议调整策略，如领取基础薪资、与投资者沟通、尝试寻找新用户或潜在买家。他们认为完全放弃可能过早，仍有机会通过改变方法让项目有所转机。

• **放弃创业，接受失败**：Quinzel和smt88认为应果断放弃不成功的项目，接受失败是创业过程的一部分。他们强调继续坚持只会消耗更多资源，而及时止损可以保留经验用于未来的新尝试。

• **通过其他途径获得稳定收入**：taraharris分享了自己的经历，建议寻找低压工作，并通过投资等方式增加收入。这种方法可以在不放弃技术背景的情况下获得财务稳定。

补充讨论：
• **情感与心理支持**：alissa_v特别提到情感和心理支持的重要性，建议在面对创业和个人困境时，给予自己一些喘息空间，避免过度压力。

• **网络与销售的重要性**：smt88和vFunct强调了网络和销售在创业中的关键作用，指出缺乏这些资源是创业失败的常见原因。

• **投资者沟通**：hardwaresofton和asimpleusecase建议与投资者保持透明，分享计划，以便在创业暂停或结束时获得理解和支持。

争议焦点：
• 是否应彻底放弃当前创业项目：部分评论者认为应果断放弃不成功的项目，而另一些人则认为仍有转机，不应过早放弃。

• 创业失败的接受度：部分评论者认为失败是创业过程的常态，而另一些人则强调从中学习并寻找新的机会。

《Slate Truck：一款售价2万美元的美国制造电动皮卡，无漆、无立体声、无触屏》——Tim Stevens  
Slate Auto公司计划推出售价不到2万美元的电动皮卡Slate Truck，预计明年投产。这款车只有两个座位，续航150英里，车身仅有一种灰色，没有立体声音响，听音乐需使用手机和蓝牙音箱。其设计极为简约，车身采用耐磨塑料而非传统油漆，内饰也强调耐用和老化美学。Slate Truck主打DIY定制，允许用户通过贴膜改变外观，以极低成本实现个性化。尽管设计简朴，但其创新制造方式吸引了包括杰夫·贝索斯在内的投资者。不过，这种极端简化是否符合美国消费者口味仍待观察。

The $20,000 American-made electric pickup with no paint, no stereo, and no touchscreen
﻿Is the market ready for a four-wheeled digital detox?
by
Tim Stevens
Apr 25, 2025, 2:20 AM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Ask just about anybody, and they’ll tell you that new cars are too expensive. In the wake of tariffs
shaking the auto industry
and with the Trump administration pledging to
kill the federal EV incentive
, that situation isn’t looking to get better soon, especially for anyone wanting something battery-powered. Changing that overly spendy status quo is going to take something radical, and it’s hard to get more radical than what Slate Auto has planned.
Meet the Slate Truck, a sub-$20,000 (after federal incentives) electric vehicle that enters production next year. It only seats two yet has a bed big enough to hold a sheet of plywood. It only does 150 miles on a charge, only comes in gray, and the only way to listen to music while driving is if you bring along your phone and a Bluetooth speaker. It is the bare minimum of what a modern car can be, and yet it’s taken three years of development to get to this point.
But this is more than bargain-basement motoring. Slate is presenting its truck as minimalist design with DIY purpose, an attempt to not just go cheap but to create a new category of vehicle with a huge focus on personalization. That design also enables a low-cost approach to manufacturing that has caught the eye of major investors, reportedly including Jeff Bezos. It’s been engineered and will be manufactured in America, but is this extreme simplification too much for American consumers?
Simplify, Then Embrace Damage
If you haven’t seen the leaks and the reports of weirdly wrapped trucks
hiding in plain sight
, the Slate Truck is the first product from Michigan-based Slate Auto. Think “American kei truck” and you’re not far off. It’s a machine designed to be extremely basic, extremely customizable, and extremely affordable. Those are not your typical design goals, but then the Slate Truck isn’t the fruit of your typical design process.
Wander through any automotive design studio anywhere in the world and you’ll inevitably come across a mood board or two, sweeping collages of striking photos meant to align the creative flows of passers-by. They’re a tool for helping a disparate design team to create a cohesive product, but where many such mood boards feature glamour shots of exotic roads and beautiful people, front and center in the Slate’s mood board was something different: a big, gray shark, covered in scrapes and scars.
“It looks like a shark that has definitely been in more than one brawl and clearly has come out ahead because it’s still swimming,” says Tisha Johnson, head of design at Slate and who formerly spent a decade at Volvo. That aesthetic, of highlighting rather than hiding battle scars, is key to the Slate ethos.
Instead of steel or aluminum, the Slate Truck’s body panels are molded of plastic. Or, as Slate calls them, “injection molded polypropylene composite material.” The theory is that this makes them more durable and scratch-resistant, if only because the lack of paint means they’re one color all the way through. Auto enthusiasts of a certain age will remember the same approach used by the now-defunct Saturn Corporation, a manufacturing technique that never caught on across the industry.
Slate continues the theme through to the upholstery, too, a heathered textile that was designed to get better looking as it wears. The idea is to lean into the aged aesthetic.
But not everybody will dig the shark theme, and so the Slate Truck is designed to be customizable to a degree never seen before on a production vehicle. Johnson says this is in contrast to the overly curated experience offered by many brands.
She says over-curation by automotive designers results in situations like premium, luxury cars that are only available in a palette of disappointingly bland colors: “There’s usually only a fraction that you actually want, and those are always more expensive,” she says.
Disparaging other brands for offering limited color choices might seem disingenuous coming from the designer of a vehicle available in a single shade. The Slate Truck, though, was designed to take advantage of the current trend of
vinyl-wrapping cars
. Its simple shape and minimal trim pieces mean that even amateurs can do the job. Slate will offer DIY kits that newbies can slap on in an afternoon and replace just as quickly based on mood.
However, the biggest benefit of this monochromatic thinking might come in production.

主要讨论点：Web应用防火墙（WAF）规则对技术内容网站的影响及其实际效果

不同观点：
• **WAF规则的必要性与平衡**：matt_heimer认为WAF规则在安全性和可用性之间需要平衡。虽然WAF可以提高安全性，但过于严苛的规则会给技术讨论型网站带来困扰，尤其是当这些规则阻止了正常技术内容时。规则的精细调整非常耗时，经常需要完全关闭某些规则集。
• **WAF引发的不必要问题**：SonOfLilit和simonw分享了由于WAF误报导致的技术问题案例，例如编程教学中某些代码关键词触发403错误，以及在技术讨论平台上因为WAF阻止了合法内容编辑。simonw特别指出，在技术写作平台上使用过于严苛的WAF是不合适的，应该通过正确的内容转义来解决问题。
• **WAF的局限性与误用**：arp242认为WAF通常是“垃圾软件”使用的工具，显示出开发者缺乏关心或能力。他指出，防止路径遍历等攻击有更好的方法，而不是依赖于这种可能对用户产生神秘负面影响的WAF。
• **对问题根源的质疑**：0xbadcafebee对是否是WAF导致403错误提出了质疑，认为有可能是其他因素触发了这个问题，不一定与WAF有关。

补充讨论：
• **具体案例与轶事**：netsharc分享了一个关于内存异常处理的轶事，强调了错误处理和工作around的荒谬性。pimanrules提到内部红队测试导致的WAF误报问题。
• **历史与技术背景**：mrgoldenbrown提到了“Scunthorpe问题”，这是一个早期的内容过滤问题案例。eniac111和righthand则提到了其他技术领域中类似的过滤问题。
• **潜在的安全隐患与讽刺**：nottorp讽刺地建议大家去寻找平台的安全漏洞，以回应平台不恰当的WAF使用策略。

争议焦点：
• WAF规则在提供安全保护的同时，是否对技术内容和正常用户操作产生了不必要的阻碍。
• 如何有效地在安全性和可用性之间找到平衡，是否应该依赖WAF来进行这种保护。

data.title: Eurorack Knob Idea
data.author: po
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种创新的Eurorack模块旋钮设计，旨在解决因空间限制而导致的模块面板混乱问题。作者与Dave Cranmer合作，设计了一个结合3.5mm插头和磁编码器（AS5600）的旋钮，通过磁铁将插头变为旋钮和接线插头的混合体。作者详细描述了制作过程，包括切割插头、嵌入磁铁、3D打印填充件以及电路设计和组装步骤。最终设计使用I2C接口读取角度数据，并可通过PWM或DAC输出模拟电压。整个设计经过多次实验和调整，最终成功实现预期功能，为Eurorack模块提供了更整洁的面板解决方案。

补充讨论：

• **用户界面与交互设计**：一些评论涉及到用户界面的设计，包括硬件旋钮和插孔的布局以及软件UI的设计，强调了直观操作和可见性的重要性。
• **技术实现与细节**：部分评论关注了具体的技术实现细节，如电路设计、兼容性和技术规范，显示了技术细节在设计中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **复杂性 vs. 简化**：一些用户认为Eurorack的魅力在于其复杂性和可编程性，而另一些用户则更倾向于简化的设计，追求更直接的操作体验。
• **创新设计的实用性**：对于提出的创新设计，一些用户认为这种设计虽然有趣，但在实际应用中可能过于复杂和昂贵，不如传统设计实用。

Eurorack Knob Idea
24 Apr 2025
Progress: Complete
Last year I designed a eurorack module, as a collaboration with Dave Cranmer. When I say designed it, I mean we got about 90% of the way there, then got distracted. With any luck, that module will get finished and released sometime soon.
But it had me thinking about Eurorack and the weird compromises people often make to fit more and more modules into a tiny case. I know a thing or two about tiny synthesizers. But my creations are often whimsical and useless. When it comes to Eurorack, where people spend crazy amounts of money on their setups, it's weird to see people compromise on the main aspect that gives it an edge over simulating the whole thing in software.
To clean up our Eurorack panels, perhaps we need a new knob idea? Watch the following video for a prototypical demo.
In essence, we're using a 3.5mm jack in front of a magnetic encoder chip, and a small magnet embedded in the plug turns it into a knob and patch cable hybrid.
The magnetic encoder in question is an AS5600. These are not the cheapest parts but they do make prototyping very easy. It has two hall sensors in an XY configuration and a dollop of DSP to give us an angle and a magnitude. They're easily available on breakout boards and have an i2c interface.
The board also comes with a specially polarised magnet with the field across the diameter instead of axially. We're not going to use that.
Building the knob
I started by taking a dremel cutting disk to the end of a TRS plug. This was just done by eye. Edge-on, it's not quite centred but it'll work fine.
This cheap plug is in fact partially hollow, and is made from plated brass.
Into this slot I glued a small neodymium magnet. It's 2mm diameter, 1mm thickness. I also bought some 2mm thickness magnets, but that would need a slightly wider slot, which would probably require a more precise cutting method.
I used a medium viscosity cyanoacrylate glue. Once set, the excess can be scraped away with a razor blade.
I turned away the threaded section, trimmed the metal tab, and 3D printed a filler piece so the back of the plug is just a straight cylinder to which we can fit a knob.
And to that, we fitted the knob. The 3D printed plastic is quite pliable, so the set screw embeds itself a little and gets a solid grip.
Circuit design
I was unsure if the tiny magnet would be sufficient, and how close it would need to be held to the soic-8 sensor chip. I did some tests, just holding this magnetic knob over one of the breakout boards.
There's both a PWM output and a DAC on the AS5600, with the idea that we can use it, once configured, to output an analog voltage. I had a assumed there was some zero-config mode that would just turn magnetic fields into voltages, but it seems we need to set it up via i2c to get any output. If that's the case, for the sake of this test we might as well just read out the angle via i2c as well.
After a few experiments I was convinced it was going to work, so I set about building a circuit board that could house the AS5600 under a TRS socket.
A common style of vertical-mount TRS socket looks like this (I believe it's a PJ398SM):
With our magnetic knob fitted, we can see that there's almost zero clearance between the tip of the TRS plug and the plane of the circuit board.
There might be a vertical-mount TRS jack out there somewhere that has enough clearance underneath it, but the through-mount pins are long enough here that we can just lift up the socket off the board. I considered 3D printing or laser-cutting a frame to elevate it, but better still is to use PCB material (FR4) as we can tack it onto the same circuit board order.
The height of the AS5600 is about 1.47mm; a 1.6mm board will work nicely. There are some diagrams in the datasheet illustrating how the magnet should be situated relative to the chip.
I stacked the two part footprints, and then laid out a second version of the socket footprint with a cutout for the chip.
I like to model the board outline exactly, with a 2mm endmill in mind, it makes it explicitly clear what we expect to receive from the board house. If you specify tight inside corners, they will probably use their judgement as to how tight a corner you were expecting. Drawing these out in KiCad is a bit tedious, but at this point I'm used to it.
I optimistically added a CH32V003 and a bunch of LEDs so we can show the value. I also chucked the usual clamping diodes and ~100K input impedance, made of 33K and 66K resistors, which divide a 0-5V signal down to 0-3.3V.
Since the encoder chip will be buried, I also added pads underneath so that if it comes to it, we can probe any leg of the chip.
The design was blasted off to China and a short while later the boards were in my hands.
Assembly and test
Assembly was uneventful. I was especially careful to get the AS5600 perfectly centred on the pads.

data.title: A Love Letter to People Who Believe in People
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者Tina对热情力量的深刻体会。从八岁时制作“粉丝俱乐部”海报，到成年后在生活和工作中遇到的几位关键人物，她意识到热情能改变人生。她的 eccentric 姨妈Hugi教会她勇敢、创意生活；她的首任老板Matthew Waldman让她明白工作环境可以充满关爱；女儿Ella的出生激励她创立自己的设计工作室；Jim Coudal让她相信自己也能实现创意想法。Tina受热情驱使，创立了Coworking空间Studiomates和晨间创意讲座CreativeMornings，通过这些社区活动，她与志同道合的人相互激励、共同成长。热情不仅改变了她自己，也影响了周围的人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对成为“粉丝”和“批评者”的不同态度及其社会影响

不同观点：
• HanClinto认为成为粉丝是积极、鼓励他人的选择，并与批评者的破坏性行为形成对比。HanClinto强调，作为粉丝能够传递热情，并带来正面的社会影响，而批评者往往是在事后挑剔别人。

• flanked-evergl引用了对现代谦逊的反思，指出如今的谦逊往往让人怀疑自己的目标，而不是努力改进。这种态度与HanClinto的观点形成对照，认为过度的自我怀疑可能导致停滞不前。

• svelle分享了个人经历，表示有一个支持自己的导师非常重要，这种积极的反馈能够深刻改变个人的职业和个性。该观点支持成为粉丝的正面作用，强调鼓励和建设性反馈的重要性。

• PaulHoule提到在社交媒体上找到支持自己的人是一种宝贵的体验，特别是在一些平台上，粉丝的热情表现得更加明显。这与HanClinto的观点相呼应，强调粉丝的热情具有感染力。

• badmonster简单赞美了文章，表达了对热情和相信他人的力量的欣赏，没有提出明显的争议。

• bicepjai承认文章对粉丝的积极描绘，但提出粉丝文化也有可能产生负面影响，特别是在某些地区，粉丝文化可能演变成具有社会和政治影响的派系和政治团体。这个观点提出了对粉丝文化的批判性思考。

• bix6同意HanClinto的观点，认为早期的热情支持非常重要，能够带动更多人的参与。

• rfl890和patcon的评论与主要讨论点无直接关系，rfl890幽默地误以为进入了某个品牌的网站，patcon则提到了对文章作者创办组织的尊重。

• felixarba简单表示成为粉丝的选择在于个人，没有深入展开。

• bookofjoe提供了文章链接的替代版本，解决了原文链接失效的问题。

• ChrisMarshallNY分享了自己对热情的态度，指出在科技行业中，许多人对热情的反应并不积极，暗示了在某些环境中，成为粉丝可能并不受欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是粉丝文化的双面性。bicepjai指出了粉丝文化可能带来的负面社会和政治影响，与其他评论中对粉丝文化的全面肯定形成对比。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对现代谦逊的反思（flanked-evergl），这提供了一个更广泛的哲学背景，讨论了谦逊与自我怀疑之间的平衡问题。
• 评论中多次提到热情和支持的感染力，以及在个人和职业发展中得到粉丝支持的重要性，强调了正面反馈的社会价值。

Tina on the transformative power of enthusiasm
When I was eight, I made a big, hand-drawn poster that said, “Do you want to join my fan club?” and put it up in the small Swiss town where I grew up.
Neighbors would ask me, “What are we going to be fans of?” and I’d say, “It doesn’t matter—it’s just about being excited.” Eight year old Tina.
Decades later, I’m still convinced that being a fan is a state of mind.
Being a fan is all about bringing the enthusiasm. It’s being a champion of possibility. It’s believing in someone. And it’s contagious. When you’re around someone who is super excited about something, it washes over you. It feels good. You can’t help but want to bring the enthusiasm, too.
This, to me, is the real transformation. Confidence is impressive, but enthusiasm can change people’s lives.
If I trace all the defining moments of my life back to their beginnings, I can always find a person with this fan state of mind: someone who believed in me, opened a door, or illuminated a new path just by being who they are.
This is a love letter to all the people who believe in us and nudge us in new directions with their enthusiasm.
To the person who showed me you can live life your way—my beloved, eccentric Aunt Hugi
She was the most creative, unique, stubborn, wild Swiss woman I have ever known. I grew up in the Swiss countryside and visiting Hugi in Zurich was always an adventure. She was a fashion designer, artist, and a true original. As I got older, I really started to appreciate how she didn’t care what people thought. She lived a courageous, creative life and inspired me to be bold, forge my own path, and break rules.
To the person who opened up a different future—my first boss, Matthew Waldman
After I earned my graphic design degree, I convinced my parents that I wanted to go to New York to find a three-month internship. I arrived on a Monday night and had an interview lined up the next morning with Matthew Waldman—the CEO of a small, now defunct design studio. Within five minutes of talking to me, he offered me a job and predicted that I would never leave New York.
Not only was he right, but his instant belief in me taught me that your boss can be enthusiastic, kind, and caring. This set the tone going forward—I would not accept anything other than a loving work environment.
To the person who nudged me to ask myself, “What am I waiting for?”—my daughter Ella
While working as a Design Director at a digital agency and pregnant with my daughter Ella, I found myself inspired to think bigger. I always wanted to run my own design studio and an urgency suddenly hit me—I was making a human, and I wanted to be a role model to them, so what was I waiting for? I started my own design studio the day she was born.
To the person who helped me realise “I can do this too”—the inspiring Jim Coudal
My blog swissmiss became quite popular, but when I had other ideas, I’d second-guess them. I’d think, Who am I to do this thing? A real epiphany came when I was watching Jim Coudal at SXSW. As he was describing his fun side projects, including The Deck Network, Layer Tennis, and Field Notes, I realized I could put my ideas into the world, too. Seeing someone create the things they want to create can give us permission to do the same.
So I did it. I knew intuitively that the people you surround yourself with change what you dream about, which led me to start the coworking space Studiomates (now known as Friends Work Here). It has been magical to see what unfolds when you gather creative, kind, driven humans in a physical space. We often find ourselves in deep, engaging conversations over coffee or lunch, which in turn has led to the founding of multiple companies, magazines and conferences. We believe in each other, and we make each other brave.
To the person who encouraged the momentum of CreativeMornings—co-founder of Mailchimp, Ben Chestnut
After experiencing the power of my coworking community, I felt inspired to share the magic. I was in a city of eight million people, but the creative communities felt fragmented and disconnected. I knew there had to be more heart-centered, creative people looking to connect. So, I decided to invite people to the space for a free breakfast and a talk. I vividly remember being made fun of for inviting people to an event at 8:30 a.m., and assuming no one would show up. I am proud to say we had 50 attendees at the first ever CreativeMornings in October of 2008.
Just four months and four events later, I received an email from Ben Chestnut, co-founder of Mailchimp, saying he and his team were big fans and he wondered if they could sponsor future events. I had never dealt with sponsors before and clumsily invited them to pay for breakfast, which turned into the most supportive and encouraging 15-year corporate partnership and friendship.

data.title: Exploiting Undefined Behavior in C/C++ Programs: The Performance Impact [pdf]
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于未定义行为（Undefined Behavior，UB）在代码优化中的作用及其相关内存模型的讨论

不同观点：
• **pcwalton 的观点**：认为文章并没有声称消除所有与未定义行为相关的推理。他通过一个代码示例（`int f() { int arr[3], i = 0; arr[3] = 5; return i; }`）指出，某些优化仍然依赖于未定义行为（UB），例如假设变量`i`没有被直接布局在数组`arr`之后。他认为文章提出的语义并非真正的“扁平内存模型”，因为这种模型应该排除上述优化，实际上他们的内存模型仍保留了对象边界的概念，只是有所简化。

• **mwkaufma 的观点**：提到通过使用LTO（Link-Time Optimization）可以恢复因禁用UB而导致的性能损失，但指出“can”在这里承担了太多期望。他认为，保证预期的优化“will”被应用是非常困难的，尤其是在依赖于间接的、容易被干扰的副作用时。

• **gitroom 的观点**：对优化如LTO可能因为构建痛苦而被团队避免表示疑问，并询问是否存在对工具链过于聪明的更深层次的不信任。他还提出一个问题，即开发者是否会为了最终产品的大幅速度提升而忍受缓慢的构建过程。

• **jonstewart 的观点**：引用了文章结论，强调在他们评估的案例中，利用UB带来的性能提升是微小的，而且即使性能下降，也可以通过编译器的小到中等修改或使用链接时优化来恢复。他对文章的结论表示赞同和支持。

补充讨论：
• 关于**LTO**（链接时优化）的讨论，各方对其有效性和实际应用中的可行性存在不同看法。mwkaufma认为LTO的效果并不稳定，而gitroom则关注开发者是否愿意为了性能而忍受缓慢的构建过程。
• **对工具链的信任问题**：gitroom提到了开发者可能对工具链的智能化存在不信任，这可能影响他们对优化的接受程度。
• **未定义行为（UB）在优化中的作用**：pcwalton认为UB在某些优化中仍起作用，而jonstewart则支持文章的观点，认为UB带来的性能提升有限，且可以通过其他方式弥补。

争议焦点：
• 未定义行为是否在优化中扮演重要角色，以及文章提出的内存模型是否真正实现了“扁平内存模型”。

data.title: Writing a Linux Debugger (2017)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
这篇文章是关于编写Linux调试器的系列教程的第一部分，主要介绍设置步骤。作者指出，尽管调试器是开发者的重要工具，但关于其工作原理和编写方法的资源较少。该系列教程旨在讲解如何编写一个Linux程序的调试器，并最终扩展为一本书。

教程分为十部分，最终代码可在GitHub上找到。调试器将支持启动、暂停、继续执行、设置断点、读写寄存器和内存、单步执行、打印源位置和回溯、处理变量等功能。作者使用C++，并专注于实现基本功能而非复杂的错误处理。

设置环境需要两个依赖项：Linenoise处理命令行输入，libelfin解析调试信息。使用fork/exec模式启动被调试程序，并通过ptrace系统调用控制和监视程序执行。ptrace允许读取寄存器、内存、单步执行等操作，是编写调试器的核心工具。文章最后简要介绍了ptrace的基本用法和执行被调试程序的步骤。
